entry.title: GTF: Omnidirectional EPI Transformer for Light Field Super-Resolution

author.name: Kunyu Li, Fei Wang, Lichao Zhang, Junjie Liu, Bihong Li

entry.summary: Presents GTF, an omnidirectional EPI Transformer for light field super-resolution that explicitly models horizontal, vertical, and diagonal epipolar plane images within a unified framework.

entry.title: VC-FeS: Viewpoint-Conditioned Feature Selection for Vehicle Re-identification in Thermal Vision

author.name: Yasod Ginige, Ransika Gunasekara, Darsha Hewavitharana, Manjula Ariyarathne, Peshala Jayasekara, Ranga Rodrigo

entry.summary: Proposes viewpoint-conditioned feature selection for vehicle re-identification in thermal images, addressing challenges from lack of color information and viewpoint variability through area-specific feature comparisons.

author.name: Rapha\"el Del\'ecluse, Hazem Wannous, Laurent Guimas

entry.summary: Reports on ICPR 2026 TVRID competition for privacy-aware top-view person re-identification using RGB-Depth from overhead cameras, with 86 identities across four viewpoints in three tracks.

entry.title: AI-Aided Advancements in Autonomous Underwater Vehicle Navigation

author.name: Guy Damari, Zeev Yampolsky, Nadav Cohen, Arup Kumar Sahoo, Jeryes Danial, Felipe O. Silva, Itzik Klein

entry.summary: Surveys AI-aided navigation advances for autonomous underwater vehicles, focusing on sensor fusion architectures integrating INS with DVL and cameras, and the emergence of learning-based approaches for dead-reckoning enhancement.

entry.title: Designing a double deep reinforcement learning selection tool for resilient demand prediction

author.name: Bilel Abderrahmane Benziane, Benoit Lardeux, Ayoub Mcharek, Maher Jridi

entry.summary: Proposes a double deep reinforcement learning agent for automatic forecasting model selection in supply chain demand prediction, with a novel early-stopping approach.

entry.title: A Regulatory Governance Framework for AI-Driven Financial Fraud Detection in U.S. Banking: Integrating OCC, SR 11-7, CFPB, and FinCEN Compliance Requirements for Model Development, Validation, and Monitoring Lifecycles

entry.title: Efficient Handwriting-Based Alzheimer,s Disease Diagnosis Using a Low-Rank Mixture of Experts Deep Learning Framework

author.name: Wu Wang, Yuang Cheng, Fouzi Harrou, Ying Sun

entry.summary: Proposes a Low-Rank Mixture of Experts framework for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis based on handwriting analysis, allowing multiple experts to specialize in different handwriting patterns.

entry.title: Resource Utilization of Differentiable Logic Gate Networks Deployed on FPGAs

author.name: Stephen Wormald, Gilon Kravatsky, Damon Woodard, Domenic Forte

entry.summary: Studies resource utilization tradeoffs (power, area, speed, accuracy) of differentiable Logic Gate Networks deployed on FPGAs across varying depth and width configurations.

entry.title: DART: A Vision-Language Foundation Model for Comprehensive Rope Condition Monitoring

author.name: Anju Rani, Daniel Ortiz-Arroyo, Petar Durdevic

entry.summary: Presents DART, a vision-language model for comprehensive rope condition monitoring that combines ViT-H/14 with Llama-3.2-3B via a novel cross-modal fusion module. Addresses the full industrial inspection workflow from severity estimation to maintenance recommendations from a single image.

entry.title: Federated Learning for Early Prediction of EV Charging Demand

author.name: Vasilis Perifanis, Foteini Nikolaidou, Nikolaos Pavlidis, Panagiotis Thomakos, Andreas Sendros

entry.summary: Studies federated learning for early prediction of EV charging demand using only plug-in metadata and first minutes of charging data. Demonstrates privacy-preserving prediction for EV network operators.

entry.title: Constrained Extreme Gradient Boosting for Adapting Reduced-Order Models

author.name: Melika Baghi, Xiao Liu, Kamran Paynabar

entry.summary: Proposes Constrained Extreme Gradient Boosting (cXGBoost) for predicting POD bases in reduced-order models as functions of system parameters, enabling adaptive basis construction.

entry.title: HUGO-CS: A Hybrid-Labeled, Uncertainty-Aware, General-Purpose, Observational Dataset for Cold Spray

author.name: Stephen Price, Kyle Miller, Marco Musto, Kenneth Kroenlein, James Saal, Kyle Tsaknopoulos, Elke A. Rundensteiner, Danielle L. Cote

entry.summary: Presents HUGO-CS, a literature-derived dataset of 4,383 cold spray experiments (30x larger than previous) with 144 features from 1,124 sources, supporting ML-driven process optimization.

entry.title: Constraint-Aware Execution Planning for Hybrid Space-Ground Compute Workloads

entry.title: DALight-3D: A Lightweight 3D U-Net for Brain Tumor Segmentation from Multi-Modal MRI

author.name: Nand Kumar Mishra, Dhruv Mishra, Dr Manu Pratap Singh

entry.summary: Presents DALight-3D, a compact 3D U-Net for brain tumor segmentation using depthwise separable convolutions, cross-slice attention, and adaptive skip fusion. Achieves competitive performance with fewer parameters.

entry.title: Vol-Mark: A Watermark for 3D Medical Volume Data Via Cubic Difference Expansion and Contrastive Learning

author.name: Jiangnan Zhu, Yuntao Wang, Shengli Pan, Yujie Gu

entry.title: On the Influence of the Feature Computation Budget on Per-Instance Algorithm Selection for Black-Box Optimization

author.name: Koen van der Blom, Diederick Vermetten

entry.summary: Studies the tradeoff between feature computation budget and per-instance algorithm selection performance in black-box optimization. Examines when computing features becomes worthwhile.

entry.title: Adapting Large Language Models to a Low-Resource Agglutinative Language: A Comparative Study of LoRA and QLoRA for Bashkir

author.name: Mullosharaf K. Arabov, Svetlana S. Khaybullina

entry.summary: Compares LoRA and QLoRA parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods for adapting LLMs to Bashkir, a low-resource Turkic language, using models ranging from DistilGPT2 to Mistral-7B. QLoRA on Mistral-7B achieved near-competitive perplexity (3.79) to full fine-tuning of GPT-2 medium (3.34). Provides practical guidance for low-resource language adaptation.

entry.title: A cross-modal network for facial expression recognition

author.name: Chunwei Tian, Jingyuan Xie, Qi Zhang, Chao Li, Wangmeng Zuo, Shichao Zhang

entry.title: Exploring Clustering Capability of Inpainting Model Embeddings for Pattern-based Individual Identification

entry.title: S-LCG: Structured Linear Congruential Generator-Based Deterministic Algorithm for Search and Optimization

entry.title: Research Summary: May 06, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is dominated by AI safety and alignment mechanistics, with several papers revealing how misalignment emerges, propagates, and can be mitigated at a geometric and representational level.

  • Feature Superposition Geometry provides a mechanistic explanation for emergent misalignment, showing fine-tuning can unintentionally amplify dangerous features via superposition
  • Model Spec Midtraining introduces a novel training phase between pretraining and RLHF that improves alignment generalization by exposing models to their own behavioral specifications
  • Specification gaming in reasoning models is shown to be exacerbated by RL training, with all tested models exploiting specifications at non-negligible rates
  • Iterative finetuning is found to be mostly idempotent under SFT/RLHF, providing reassuring evidence against catastrophic model collapse

In mechanistic interpretability, Llama-3.1-8B is shown to reuse a generic base-10 addition circuit for cyclic concept arithmetic. Compute Optimal Tokenization trains 988 BLT models revealing that token compression rate has a compute-optimal sweet spot affecting scaling behavior.

  • Guard model safety geometry collapses under benign fine-tuning, posing critical risks for agentic deployment pipelines
  • Proteo-R1 combines reasoning LLMs with generative protein design in a dual-expert architecture
  • InfoLaw extends scaling laws to account for data quality mixtures and repetition
  • Systematic verification errors in RLVR cause qualitatively different failure modes (delay, plateau, collapse) compared to random noise

entry.title: Model Spec Midtraining: Improving How Alignment Training Generalizes

author.name: Chloe Li, Sara Price, Samuel Marks, Jon Kutasov

entry.title: Towards Understanding Specification Gaming in Reasoning Models

author.name: Kei Nishimura-Gasparian, Robert McCarthy, David Lindner

entry.summary: Systematically studies specification gaming in LLM agents, finding all tested models exploit specifications at non-negligible rates. Key findings: RL reasoning training substantially increases specification gaming, Grok 4 shows highest rates while Claude models show lowest, and specification gaming increases with RL training and longer reasoning.

entry.title: Minimizing Collateral Damage in Activation Steering

author.name: Tam Nguyen, Tu Anh Nguyen, Sina Alemohammad, Richard G. Baraniuk

entry.summary: Provides mathematical formalization of collateral damage in activation steering and introduces a constrained optimization framework. Minimizes unintended changes in non-target feature directions during LLM behavior control.

entry.title: Concepts Whisper While Syntax Shouts: Spectral Anti-Concentration and the Dual Geometry of Transformer Representations

author.name: Pratyush Acharya, Nuraj Rimal, Habish Dhakal

entry.summary: Tests whether causal inner products enable cross-lingual concept transport across 17 models and 4 language pairs, finding that Whitened Causal Alignment is indistinguishable from spectral regularization alone. Discovers a 'dual geometry' where concept directions anti-concentrate in spectral tails while syntax concentrates in top eigenvectors. Reveals fundamental structure of transformer representations.

entry.title: RefusalGuard: Geometry-Preserving Fine-Tuning for Safety in LLMs

author.name: Sadia Asif, Mohammad Mohammadi Amiri

entry.summary: RefusalGuard investigates representation-level mechanisms of alignment degradation during fine-tuning. Shows that standard fine-tuning induces systematic drift in safety representations, distorts geometric structure, and creates interference between task optimization and safety features. Proposes geometry-preserving fine-tuning to maintain safety.

entry.title: What Single-Prompt Accuracy Misses: A Multi-Variant Reliability Audit of Language Models

author.name: Ranit Karmakar, Jayita Chatterjee

entry.summary: This paper audits 15 open-weight language models across prompt variants, revealing that single-prompt accuracy benchmarks miss critical reliability failures - switching calibration definitions changes results dramatically, and prompt perturbation spread varies significantly across models.

entry.title: Efficient Preference Poisoning Attack on Offline RLHF

author.name: Chenye Yang, Weiyu Xu, Lifeng Lai

entry.summary: Studies preference poisoning attacks on DPO by developing efficient label-flip attack methods (BAL-A and BMP-A) that exploit a key property: flipping one preference label induces a parameter-independent gradient shift.

entry.title: Reward Hacking Benchmark: Measuring Exploits in LLM Agents with Tool Use

author.name: Kunvar Thaman

entry.summary: Introduces the Reward Hacking Benchmark (RHB) for evaluating LLM agents with tool access, featuring multi-step tasks with naturalistic shortcut opportunities. Evaluates 13 frontier models finding exploit rates from 0% (Claude Sonnet 4.5) to 13.9% (DeepSeek-R1-Zero).

entry.title: DGPO: Distribution Guided Policy Optimization for Fine Grained Credit Assignment

author.name: Hongbo Jin, Rongpeng Zhu, Zhongjing Du, Xu Jiang, Jingqi Tian, Qiaoman Zhang, Jiayu Ding

entry.summary: Proposes Distribution Guided Policy Optimization (DGPO), a critic-free RL framework that reinterprets distribution deviation as a guiding signal for fine-grained credit assignment in LLM reasoning. Addresses limitations of GRPO's coarse sequence-level credit assignment and KL divergence instability.

entry.title: RLDX-1 Technical Report

author.name: Dongyoung Kim, Huiwon Jang, Myungkyu Koo, Suhyeok Jang, Taeyoung Kim, Beomjun Kim, Byungjun Yoon, Changsung Jang, Daewon Choi, Dongsu Han, Donguk Lee, Heeseung Kwon, Hojin Jeon, Jaehyun Kang, Jaekyoung Bae, Jihyuk Lee, Jimin Lee, John Won, Joonwoo Ahn, Junhyeong Park, Junyoung Sung, Kyungmin Lee, Minseong Han, Minsung Yoon, Sejune Joo, Seonil Son, Seungcheol Park, Seunggeun Cho, Seungjun Moon, Seungku Kim, Yonghoon Dong, Yongjin Cho, Youngchan Kim, Chang Hwan Kim, Dohyeon Kim, Hazel Lee, Heecheol Kim, Hensen Ahn, Hyungkyu Ryu, Hyunsoo Choi, Hyunsoo Shin, Jaeheon Jung, Jaewoo Kim, Jinwook Kim, Joochul Chang, Joonsoo Kim, Junghun Park, Jungwoo Park, Junho Cho, Junhyeok Park, Junwon Lee, Kangwook Lee, Kwanghoon Kim, Kyoungwhan Choe, Manoj Bhadu, Nayoung Oh, Sangjun Kim, Sangwoo Kim, Seunghoon Shim, Seunghyun Kim, Seungjun Lee, Seungyup Ka, Sungryol Yang, Wook Jung, Yashu Shukla, Yeonjae Lee, Yeonwoo Bae, Jinwoo Shin

entry.summary: Introduces RLDX-1, a general-purpose robotic policy for dexterous manipulation built on Multi-Stream Action Transformer (MSAT), integrating vision, language, motion awareness, memory, and physical sensing through modality-specific streams with cross-modal attention. Addresses VLA limitations in complex real-world tasks.

entry.title: Exposing LLM Safety Gaps Through Mathematical Encoding:New Attacks and Systematic Analysis

author.name: Haoyu Zhang, Mohammad Zandsalimy, Shanu Sushmita

entry.summary: Shows that encoding harmful prompts as mathematical problems (set theory, formal logic, quantum mechanics) bypasses LLM safety filters at 46-56% success rate across 8 models. Key finding: effectiveness depends on deep reformulation by a helper LLM, not mere mathematical formatting.

entry.title: LLM Output Detectability and Task Performance Can be Jointly Optimized

author.name: Koshiro Saito, Ryuto Koike, Masahiro Kaneko, Naoaki Okazaki

entry.summary: Proposes PUPPET, a framework using reinforcement learning to jointly optimize LLM watermark detectability and downstream task performance. Shows that watermarked text can maintain or improve task quality while remaining detectable.

entry.title: The Cylindrical Representation Hypothesis for Language Model Steering

author.name: Lang Gao, Jinghui Zhang, Wei Liu, Fengxian Ji, Chenxi Wang, Zirui Song, Akash Ghosh, Youssef Mohamed, Preslav Nakov, Xiuying Chen

entry.summary: Proposes the Cylindrical Representation Hypothesis (CRH) as an extension of the Linear Representation Hypothesis for understanding model steering. Formalizes how overlapping concept contributions yield sample-specific axis-orthogonal structure.

entry.title: DALPHIN: Benchmarking Digital Pathology AI Copilots Against Pathologists on an Open Multicentric Dataset

author.name: Carlijn Lems, Sander Moonemans, Nat\'alie Klub\'i\v{c}kov\'a, Biagio Brattoli, Taebum Lee, Seokhwi Kim, Veronica Vilaplana, Laura Pons, Sapir Hochman, Mauricio Eduardo Su\'arez-Franck, Pedro Luis Fernandez, Julius Drachneris, Donatas Petroska, Renaldas Augulis, Arvydas Laurinavicius, Domingos Oliveira, Diana Montezuma, Anouk B. Bouwmeester, Dominique van Midden, Anne-Marie Vos, Shoko Vos, Jolique van Ipenburg, Maschenka Balkenhol, Koen Winkler, Iris Nagtegaal, Konnie Hebeda, Uta Flucke, Katrien Gr\"unberg, Josef Skopal, Brinder S. Chohan, Jordi Temprana-Salvador, Enrico Munari, Luca Cima, Giulia Querzoli, Yosamin Gonzalez Belisario, Jaeike W. Faber, Geert J. L. H. van Leenders, Jan H. von der Th\"usen, Lodewijk A. A. Brosens, Ronald R. de Krijger, Pieter Wesseling, Sandrine Florquin, Mateusz Maniewski, Adam Kowalewski, Robert Barna, Dina Tiniakos, Joan Lop Gros, Rogier Donders, Jake S. F. Maurits, Ming Yang Lu, Chengkuan Chen, Faisal Mahmood, Jeroen van der Laak, Nadieh Khalili, Fr\'ed\'erique Meeuwsen, Francesco Ciompi

entry.summary: DALPHIN is the first multicentric open benchmark for pathology AI copilots, testing GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and PathChat+ against 31 pathologists across 1236 images from 300 cases spanning 130 diagnoses and 14 subspecialties.

entry.title: Position: Safety and Fairness in Agentic AI Depend on Interaction Topology, Not on Model Scale or Alignment

author.name: Tanav Singh Bajaj, Nikhil Singh, Karan Anand, Eishkaran Singh

entry.summary: Position paper arguing that safety in multi-agent AI systems is determined by interaction topology (agent ordering, information flow) rather than individual model scale or alignment, identifying three topology-driven pathologies.

entry.title: Trustworthy AI Suffers from Invariance Conflicts and Causality is The Solution

author.name: Ruta Binkyte, Ivaxi Sheth, Zhijing Jin, Mohammad Havaei, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Mario Fritz

entry.summary: Position paper arguing causality is necessary to understand and balance trustworthy AI trade-offs (fairness, robustness, privacy, explainability), re-interpreting these as incompatible invariance requirements under different data-generating process changes. Authors include Bernhard Schölkopf.

entry.title: Earth System Foundation Model (ESFM): A unified framework for heterogeneous data integration and forecasting

author.name: Firat Ozdemir, Yun Cheng, Salman Mohebi, Fanny Lehmann, Simon Adamov, Zhenyi Zhang, Leonardo Trentini, Dana Grund, Oliver Fuhrer, Torsten Hoefler, Siddhartha Mishra, Sebastian Schemm, Benedikt Soja, Mathieu Salzmann

entry.summary: Introduces ESFM (Earth System Foundation Model), a fully open model extending Aurora's 3D Swin UNet backbone to handle diverse Earth system datasets including satellite data with missing values and station data. Adds axial attention for improved spatial modeling.

entry.title: LLM Ghostbusters: Surgical Hallucination Suppression via Adaptive Unlearning

author.name: Joseph Spracklen, Pedram Aghazadeh, Farinaz Koushanfar, Murtuza Jadliwala

entry.summary: Proposes adaptive unlearning method to suppress LLM hallucinations, specifically targeting package hallucination in code generation (slopsquatting). Surgically removes hallucinated package knowledge without degrading model utility.

entry.title: The Case for ESM3 as a General-Purpose AI Model with Systemic Risk Under the EU AI Act

author.name: Taro Qureshi, Jacob Griffith, Koen Holtman, Marcel Mir Teijeiro, Ze Shen Chin, Rokas Gipi\v{s}kis

entry.summary: Examines whether ESM3 (a biological foundation model) should be classified as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk under the EU AI Act. Maps ESM3 to the biorisk chain and concludes it's desirable but not currently regulated under the Act. Proposes remedies for this regulatory gap.

entry.title: Stochastic Sparse Attention for Memory-Bound Inference

author.name: Kyle Lee, Corentin Delacour, Kevin Callahan-Coray, Kyle Jiang, Can Yaras, Samet Oymak, Tathagata Srimani, Kerem Y. Camsari

entry.summary: SANTA (Stochastic Additive No-mulT Attention) sparsifies value-cache access during autoregressive decoding by sampling indices from post-softmax distribution and aggregating only those value rows. Achieves 1.5x attention kernel speedup over FlashInfer/FlashDecoding while maintaining accuracy. Provides unbiased estimation with stratified sampling for variance reduction.

entry.title: Reference-Sampled Boltzmann Projection for KL-Regularized RLVR: Target-Matched Weighted SFT, Finite One-Shot Gaps, and Policy Mirror Descent

author.name: Yao Shu, Chenxing Wei, Hongbin Lin, Shuang Qiu, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: Identifies the precise weighted-SFT objective whose induced policy matches the KL-regularized RLVR optimizer, proving finite one-shot gaps and connecting to policy mirror descent for reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards.

entry.title: ZeRO-Prefill: Zero Redundancy Overheads in MoE Prefill Serving

author.name: Zhaoyuan Su, Olatunji Ruwase, Karthik Ganesan, Aurick Qiao, Samyam Rajbhandari, Juncheng Yang, Yue Cheng, Yuxiong He

entry.summary: Proposes ZeRO-Prefill for efficient MoE model serving of prefill-only workloads (classification, recommendation, verification). Decouples expert placement from synchronous activation routing to eliminate redundant computation inherited from the decoding era.

entry.title: Graph Reconstruction from Differentially Private GNN Explanations

author.name: Rishi Raj Sahoo, Jyotirmaya Shivottam, Subhankar Mishra

entry.summary: Demonstrates that differentially private GNN explanations can be attacked to reconstruct hidden graph structure by recasting DP noise as a DDPM forward step, enabling reverse diffusion-based reconstruction. Shows DP alone is insufficient for protecting graph privacy.

entry.title: Compared to What? Baselines and Metrics for Counterfactual Prompting

author.name: Zihao Yang, Mosh Levy, Yoav Goldberg, Byron C. Wallace

entry.summary: Argues that counterfactual prompting studies (measuring bias, CoT faithfulness) are confounded because every edit bundles the variable of interest with incidental surface-form variation. Shows 14.9% flip rates from gender changes in MedQA are indistinguishable from mere paraphrasing.

entry.title: Only Say What You Know: Calibration-Aware Generation for Long-Form Factuality

author.name: Wen Luo, Guangyue Peng, Liang Wang, Nan Yang, Wei Li, Yuhan Song, Shaohang Wei, Feifan Song, Furu Wei, Houfeng Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Exploration-Commitment Decoupling paradigm for reducing hallucinations in reasoning models, separating knowledge exploration from final commitment. Enables models to explore freely while answering cautiously.

entry.title: Accurate Legal Reasoning at Scale: Neuro-Symbolic Offloading and Structural Auditability for Robust Legal Adjudication

author.name: Stanis{\l}aw S\'ojka, Witold Kowalczyk

entry.summary: Proposes Amortized Intelligence, a neuro-symbolic approach translating legal text into deterministic graph representations (DACL) for legal adjudication. Outperforms GPT-5.2 and Gemini 3 Pro on consistency.

entry.title: GR-Ben: A General Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Process Reward Models

author.name: Zhouhao Sun, Xuan Zhang, Xiao Ding, Bibo Cai, Li Du, Kai Xiong, Xinran Dai, Fei Zhang, weidi tang, Zhiyuan Kan, Yang Zhao, Bing Qin, Ting Liu

entry.summary: Introduces GR-Ben, a benchmark for evaluating process reward models (PRMs) across science and logic reasoning domains (9 subdomains), addressing the current over-focus on math-only PRM evaluation.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Reasoning Improves Compute Efficiency: Pareto-Optimal Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Florian Valentin Wunderlich, Lars Benedikt Kaesberg, Jan Philip Wahle, Terry Ruas, Bela Gipp

entry.summary: Provides systematic analysis of inference scaling strategies (self-consistency, self-refinement, multi-agent debate, mixture-of-agents) across 34 configurations and 100+ experiments, finding Pareto-optimal compute-performance tradeoffs.

entry.title: T$^2$PO: Uncertainty-Guided Exploration Control for Stable Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haixin Wang, Hejie Cui, Chenwei Zhang, Xin Liu, Shuowei Jin, Shijie Geng, Xinyang Zhang, Nasser Zalmout, Zhenyu Shi, Yizhou Sun

entry.summary: Proposes T²PO, an uncertainty-guided framework for stabilizing multi-turn agentic RL training by controlling exploration at both token and turn levels, monitoring when actions are low-information.

entry.title: Distilling Long-CoT Reasoning through Collaborative Step-wise Multi-Teacher Decoding

author.name: Taewon Yun, Jisu Shin, Jeonghwan Choi, Seunghwan Bang, Hwanjun Song

entry.summary: Introduces CoRD, a collaborative multi-teacher decoding framework that synthesizes reasoning trajectories step-wise from multiple heterogeneous large reasoning models using perplexity-based scoring and beam search. Enables diverse teacher models to jointly construct coherent reasoning chains for distillation.

entry.title: StyleShield: Exposing the Fragility of AIGC Detectors through Continuous Controllable Style Transfer

author.name: Guantian Zheng

entry.summary: Introduces StyleShield, a flow matching framework for continuous text style transfer that exposes the fragility of AI-generated content detectors. Operates in continuous token embedding space via DiT backbone, demonstrating that AIGC detection boundaries are dissolving.

entry.title: Component-Aware Self-Speculative Decoding in Hybrid Language Models

author.name: Hector Borobia, Elies Segu\'i-Mas, Guillermina Tormo-Carb\'o

entry.summary: Introduces component-aware self-speculative decoding for hybrid language models (SSM+attention), exploiting internal architectural heterogeneity by using the SSM/linear-attention subgraph as a zero-cost internal drafter.

entry.title: Protein-Conditioned Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning for Full-Length mRNA Design

author.name: Zixi Shao, Tao Wang, Yibei Xiao, Tianyi Huang

entry.summary: ProMORNA proposes a multi-objective reinforcement learning framework for designing full-length mRNA sequences from protein sequences, using BART encoder-decoder pre-trained on 6M protein-mRNA pairs and Multi-Objective Group Relative Policy Optimization. Balances stability, translation efficiency, and immune safety simultaneously. Demonstrates results on firefly luciferase target.

entry.title: Probe-Geometry Alignment: Erasing the Cross-Sequence Memorization Signature Below Chance

author.name: Anamika Paul Rupa, Anietie Andy

entry.summary: Demonstrates that behavioral unlearning in LLMs leaves internal memorization traces recoverable by adversarial probes, and shows these can be surgically removed. Uses leave-one-out cross-sequence probes to test memorization signature generalization. The memorization-specific gaps are consistent across Pythia-70M, GPT-2, and Mistral-7B.

entry.title: Architectural Obsolescence of Unhardened Agentic-AI Runtimes

author.name: Alfredo Metere

entry.summary: Demonstrates that OpenClaw, the most engineered agentic-AI gateway, catches none of four critical action divergence types (gate-bypass, audit-forgery, host failure, wrong-target) with 0.000 recall. Identifies seven runtime structures needed for safety. Tests across 1600 samples and ten LLMs.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Hidden-State Dynamics as a Signature of Internal Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Kotaro Furuya, Takahito Tanimura

entry.summary: Investigates spatiotemporal hidden-state dynamics in large reasoning models, finding that successful reasoning trajectories exhibit broad temporal dynamics with localized layer-wise concentration. This pattern is weaker in non-reasoning models and knowledge-heavy domains. Formalizes this as 'Spatiotemporal Reasoning Signatures' to distinguish genuine computation from verbosity.

entry.title: Principles and Guidelines for Randomized Controlled Trials in AI Evaluation

author.name: Christopher Kelly, Angelica Chowdhury, Alexandra Campili, Bimpe Ayoola, Devin Barbour, Thomas Chen Dawson, Ze Shen Chin, Rokas Gipi\v{s}kis

entry.summary: Establishes a foundational framework for standardizing randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in AI evaluation, extending established experimental practices with 33 guidelines covering transparency, repeatability, and verification for AI evaluation contexts.

entry.title: The Causal Description Gap: Information-Theoretic Separations Across Pearl's Hierarchy

author.name: Seyed Morteza Emadi

entry.summary: Formalizes the quantitative gap between levels of Pearl's causal hierarchy using Kolmogorov complexity, constructing SCMs where observational descriptions are constant-length but interventional answer oracles require Θ(n²) bits.

entry.title: AI-Generated Smells: An Analysis of Code and Architecture in LLM and Agent-Driven Development

author.name: Yuecai Zhu, Nikolaos Tsantalis, Peter C. Rigby

entry.summary: Systematic audit of technical debt in AI-generated code reveals a 'Reasoning-Complexity Trade-off' where more capable models generate increasingly bloated and coupled code, establishing a 'Volume-Quality Inverse Law'.

entry.title: Generate, Filter, Control, Replay: A Comprehensive Survey of Rollout Strategies for LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Rohan Surana, Gagan Mundada, Xunyi Jiang, Chuhan Wang, Zhenwei Tang, Difan Jiao, Zihan Huang, Yuxin Xiong, Junda Wu, Sheldon Yu, Xintong Li, Raghav Jain, Nikki Kuang, Sizhe Zhou, Bowen Jin, Zhendong Chu, Tong Yu, Ryan Rossi, Kuan-Hao Huang, Jingbo Shang, Jiawei Han, Julian McAuley

entry.summary: Comprehensive survey of rollout strategies for RL-based post-training of reasoning LLMs, introducing the Generate-Filter-Control-Replay (GFCR) lifecycle taxonomy. Provides unified notation and modular decomposition of rollout pipelines that are often underreported in existing work.

entry.title: Learning Dynamics of Zeroth-Order Optimization: A Kernel Perspective

author.name: Zhe Li, Bicheng Ying, Zidong Liu, Haibo Yang

entry.summary: Explains the paradox of zeroth-order methods working well for LLM fine-tuning despite theoretical dimension-dependent slowdowns, through the lens of Neural Tangent Kernel analysis. Shows the eNTK naturally emerges as the key term governing ZO SGD learning dynamics.

entry.title: Understanding Self-Supervised Learning via Latent Distribution Matching

author.name: Fabian A Mikulasch, Friedemann Zenke

entry.summary: Proposes a unified theoretical framework for self-supervised learning as latent distribution matching (LDM), unifying contrastive, non-contrastive, and predictive SSL methods. Derives novel Bayesian filtering model for timeseries.

entry.title: Memorization In Stable Diffusion Is Unexpectedly Driven by CLIP Embeddings

author.name: Bumjun Kim, Albert No

entry.summary: Reveals that in Stable Diffusion memorization, CLIP padding embeddings (duplicating end-of-text embeddings) strongly drive memorization while prompt embeddings contribute minimally. Shows unexpected role of structural token embeddings.

entry.title: Workspace-Bench 1.0: Benchmarking AI Agents on Workspace Tasks with Large-Scale File Dependencies

author.name: Zirui Tang, Xuanhe Zhou, Yumou Liu, Linchun Li, Weizheng Wang, Hongzhang Huang, Jun Zhou, Jiachen Song, Shaoli Yu, Jinqi Wang, Zihang Zhou, Hongyi Zhou, Yuting Lv, Jinyang Li, Jiashuo Liu, Ruoyu Chen, Chunwei Liu, GuoLiang Li, Jihua Kang, Fan Wu

entry.summary: Introduces Workspace-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on tasks requiring reasoning over large-scale file dependencies across realistic workspaces (20,476 files, up to 20GB, 388 tasks). Includes 5 worker profiles with 74 file types and dependency graphs.

entry.title: Auditing demographic bias in AI-based emergency police dispatch: a cross-lingual evaluation of eleven large language models

author.name: William Guey, Wei Zhang, Pierrick Bougault, Yi Wang, Bertan Ucar, Vitor D. de Moura, Jos\'e O. Gomes

entry.summary: Introduces a cross-lingual audit framework for demographic bias in LLM-based emergency dispatch, testing 11 frontier models across 19,800 outputs. Finds systematic demographic bias when incident severity is ambiguous.

entry.title: Counting as a minimal probe of language model reliability

author.name: Tianxiang Dai, Jonathan Fan

entry.summary: Introduces Stable Counting Capacity as a minimal probe for LLM reliability, measuring procedural rule-following independent of knowledge or semantics. Shows across 100+ model variants that counting failures predict broader reliability issues.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems through Orchestration Traces

author.name: Chenchen Zhang

entry.summary: Studies RL for LLM-based multi-agent systems through orchestration traces, identifying three technical axes: reward design (8 families), credit assignment (8 signal-bearing nodes), and scalability challenges.

entry.title: Large Language Models are Universal Reasoners for Visual Generation

author.name: Sucheng Ren, Chen Chen, Zhenbang Wang, Liangchen Song, Xiangxin Zhu, Alan Yuille, Liang-Chieh Chen, Jiasen Lu

entry.summary: Proposes UniReasoner, which leverages an LLM as a universal reasoner to bridge the understanding-generation gap in text-to-image systems. The LLM generates a coarse draft then iteratively verifies and corrects it.

entry.title: Training Model to Predict Its Own Generalization: A Preliminary Study

author.name: Tianyi (Alex) Qiu

entry.summary: Studies training LLMs to predict their own generalization behavior (e.g., what happens after fine-tuning on specific data). Shows promise on emergent misalignment prediction but hasn't validated on truly surprising generalization cases.

entry.title: The Model Knows, the Decoder Finds: Future Value Guided Particle Power Sampling

author.name: Tu Nguyen, Rasul Tutunov, Xiaotong Ji, Matthieu Zimmer

entry.summary: Introduces Auxiliary Particle Power Sampling (APPS), a blockwise particle algorithm for biasing LLM decoding toward correct multi-step solutions without additional training. Uses power sampling with future-value guidance to efficiently locate high-probability modes.

entry.title: ELAS: Efficient Pre-Training of Low-Rank Large Language Models via 2:4 Activation Sparsity

author.name: Jiaxi Li, Lu Yin, Li Shen, Jinjin Xu, Yuhui Liu, Wenwu Wang, Shiwei Liu, Xilu Wang

entry.summary: Proposes ELAS, combining low-rank training with 2:4 structured activation sparsity for efficient LLM pre-training. Applies sparsity to activations rather than weights to reduce memory while leveraging GPU hardware support.

entry.title: Tracing the Dynamics of Refusal: Exploiting Latent Refusal Trajectories for Robust Jailbreak Detection

author.name: Xulin Hu, Che Wang, Wei Yang Bryan Lim, Jianbo Gao, Zhong Chen

entry.summary: Proposes SALO for jailbreak detection by exploiting dynamic refusal trajectories in LLM latent representations, showing these upstream signatures persist even when terminal signals are suppressed by attacks.

entry.title: Enhanced LLM Reasoning by Optimizing Reward Functions with Search-Driven Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Arash Ahmadi (Mike), Sarah Sharif (Mike), Yaser (Mike), Banad

entry.summary: Introduces a search-driven framework that treats reward function specification as an optimization target for RL-based reasoning improvement. Uses frontier LLMs to generate candidate reward functions validated through short GRPO training runs.

entry.title: ContextualJailbreak: Evolutionary Red-Teaming via Simulated Conversational Priming

author.name: Mario Rodr\'iguez B\'ejar, Francisco J. Cort\'es-Delgado, S. Braghin, Jose L. Hern\'andez-Ramos

entry.summary: Introduces ContextualJailbreak, an evolutionary approach to multi-turn jailbreaking that optimizes conversational priming strategies through automated mutation of attack scaffolds.

entry.title: VisInject: Disruption != Injection -- A Dual-Dimension Evaluation of Universal Adversarial Attacks on Vision-Language Models

author.name: Pang Liu, Yingjie Lao

entry.summary: VisInject proposes a dual-dimension evaluation framework distinguishing between model output perturbation (Influence) and actual target concept emission (Precise Injection) in adversarial attacks on vision-language models. Shows that reported 60-80% attack success rates conflate these two distinct events. Introduces more rigorous evaluation using Ratcliff-Obershelp drift scoring and ordinal categorical assessment.

entry.title: HeadQ: Model-Visible Distortion and Score-Space Correction for KV-Cache Quantization

author.name: Jorge L. Ruiz Williams

entry.summary: Proposes HeadQ for KV-cache quantization that measures error in model-visible coordinates (score space for keys, A²-weighted for values) rather than storage-space reconstruction, achieving better attention preservation.

entry.title: A Theoretical Game of Attacks via Compositional Skills

author.name: Xinbo Wu, Huan Zhang, Abhishek Umrawal, Lav R. Varshney

entry.summary: Formalizes the attacker-defender game in LLM adversarial prompting, designs theoretical best-response attack strategy related to existing methods, characterizes equilibria, and derives provably optimal defense strategy. Shows inherent attacker advantages.

entry.title: Less is More: Geometric Unlearning for LLMs with Minimal Data Disclosure

author.name: Chenchen Tan, Xinghao Li, Shujie Cui, Youyang Qu, Cunjian Chen, Longxiang Gao

entry.summary: Proposes Geometric Unlearning (GU) for LLMs that operates on prompt-time planning states without access to original training data, enabling selective content removal for privacy compliance.

entry.title: Segment-Aligned Policy Optimization for Multi-Modal Reasoning

author.name: Lei Gao, Zhuoming Li, Mengxi Jia, Jiakang Yuan, Hongbo Sun, Hao Sun, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: Proposes Segment-Aligned Policy Optimization (SAPO) that treats coherent reasoning steps as fundamental units for policy updates in multi-modal reasoning, with step-wise MDP abstraction and segment-level value estimation.

entry.title: Controllable and Verifiable Process Data Synthesis for Process Reward Models

author.name: Yinghui Chi, Lucien Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a controllable framework for synthesizing process supervision data for Process Reward Models. Constructs correct symbolic chains, injects template-aware errors, recomputes subsequent steps, and verifies correctness - creating paired trajectories for PRM training.

entry.title: Deciphering Shortcut Learning from an Evolutionary Game Theory Perspective

author.name: Xiayang Li, Kuo Gai, Shihua Zhang

entry.summary: Analyzes shortcut learning through evolutionary game theory, modeling data samples as players with neural tangent features as strategies. Shows GD leads to shortcut subnetwork optimization while SGD optimizes core subnetworks.

entry.title: AcademiClaw: When Students Set Challenges for AI Agents

author.name: Junjie Yu, Pengrui Lu, Weiye Si, Hongliang Lu, Jiabao Wu, Kaiwen Tao, Kun Wang, Lingyu Yang, Qiran Zhang, Xiuting Guo, Xuanyu Wang, Yang Wang, Yanjie Wang, Yi Yang, Zijian Hu, Ziyi Yang, Zonghan Zhou, Binghao Qiang, Borui Zhang, Chenning Li, Enchang Zhang, Feifan Chen, Feng Jian, Fengyin Sun, Hao Qiu, Hao Zheng, Haoran Zhu, Hongyu Liu, Jianbin Deng, Jiaxin Song, Jiaying Chi, Jiayou Shi, Jie Fang, Jinghui Zhong, Jingyu Zhou, Jinze Li, Junfeng Yi, Junyan Yu, Junzhi Xue, Ni Song, Pengyi Chen, Qi Chen, Quansheng Li, Rui Tao, Shenghai Gong, Shenhang Lu, Tianqi Shen, Tianxiang Zhu, Tiehan Kang, Tingyu Li, Wendi Wu, Xiao Shen, Xiao Zhou, Xiaotao Zhang, Xinrong Li, Xuankun Yang, Xun Zhang, Yan Li, Ye Lu, Yi Wang, Yibo Zhou, Yichi Zhang, Yihao Sun, Yijun Huang, Yixin Zhu, Yixuan Wu, Yuchen Sun, Yue Wu, Yuheng Sun, Yukun Li, Yutian Tu, Yuxuan Qin, Yuzhuo Wu, Zeyu Li, Zhengyu Lou, Zhenning Ran, Zizhu He, Pengfei Liu

entry.summary: Introduces AcademiClaw, a bilingual benchmark of 80 complex long-horizon tasks from university students' real academic workflows that current AI agents cannot solve. Spans 25+ domains including olympiad math, GPU-intensive RL, and full-stack debugging.

entry.title: Co-Generative De Novo Functional Protein Design

author.name: Xinrui Chen, Yizhen Luo, Siqi Fan, Zaiqing Nie

entry.summary: Proposes CodeFP, a co-generative protein language model that simultaneously decodes sequence and structure tokens for de novo functional protein design. Uses functional local structures for enriched semantic encoding.

entry.title: E-MIA: Exam-Style Black-Box Membership Inference Attacks against RAG Systems

author.name: Zelin Guan, Shengda Zhuo, Zeyan Li, Jinchun He, Wangjie Qiu, Zhiming Zheng, Shuqiang Huang

entry.summary: Introduces E-MIA, exam-style black-box membership inference attacks against RAG systems that can determine whether a document is in the retrieval corpus through carefully crafted query interactions.

entry.title: CLEAR: Revealing How Noise and Ambiguity Degrade Reliability in LLMs for Medicine

author.name: Kevin H. Guo, Chao Yan, Avinash Baidya, Katherine Brown, Xiang Goa, Juming Xiong, Zhijun Yin, Bradley A. Malin

entry.summary: Introduces CLEAR framework assessing how ambiguity, decision-space presentation, and uncertainty affect LLM medical reasoning. Tests 17 LLMs and reveals degradation with more plausible answers and sensitivity to semantic framing.

entry.title: When Less is Enough: Efficient Inference via Collaborative Reasoning

author.name: Yilei Chen, Sharut Gupta, Yannis Paschalidis, Ayush Sekhari, Aldo Pacchiano

entry.summary: Introduces DUET, a collaborative inference framework where a capable model produces reasoning signals and a lightweight model generates final answers. Uses length-penalized joint optimization to decompose inference stages.

entry.title: Are we Doomed to an AI Race? Why Self-Interest Could Drive Countries Towards a Moratorium on Superintelligence

author.name: Edward Roussel, Lode Lauwaert, Torben Swoboda, Grant Ramsey, Risto Uuk, Leonard Dung

entry.summary: Uses game theory to argue that a moratorium on Artificial Superintelligence can be in states' self-interest. Models show that as perceived cost of loss of control increases, mutual moratorium becomes a stable equilibrium.

entry.title: Active Reasoning Vision-Language Models via Sequential Experimental Design

author.name: Anjie Liu, Ziqin Gong, Yan Song, Yuxiang Chen, Xiaolong Liu, Hengtong Lu, Kaike Zhang, Chen Wei

entry.summary: Frames visual perception in VLMs as sequential experimental design, applying Bayesian optimal experimental design to balance spatial coverage against resolution in gigapixel images. Presents a training-free inference strategy.

entry.title: Focus on the Core: Empowering Diffusion Large Language Models by Self-Contrast

author.name: Jinyuan Feng, Xin Yu, Yiqun Chen, Xiaochi Wei, Yan Gao, Yi Wu, Yao Hu, Zhiqiang Pu

entry.summary: Proposes FoCore for Diffusion Large Language Models that identifies high-information-density tokens and explicitly conditions on them. Shows HD tokens exhibit early-decoding tendency, converging before surrounding tokens.

entry.title: Verbal-R3: Verbal Reranker as the Missing Bridge between Retrieval and Reasoning

author.name: Sangkwon Park, Donghun Kang, Jisoo Mok, Sungroh Yoon

entry.summary: Verbal-R3 introduces 'Verbal Annotations' - analytic narratives that explicitly articulate logical connections between search queries and retrieved contexts - as a bridge between retrieval and LLM reasoning in RAG systems. The framework uses a Generator and Verbal Reranker that iteratively refines these annotations. Demonstrates substantial improvements in accuracy and contextual grounding.

entry.title: Model Merging: Foundations and Algorithms

author.name: Donato Crisostomi

entry.summary: PhD thesis studying model merging as an alternative paradigm to training models independently, combining networks directly in weight space without requiring original training data. Introduces C²M³ for cycle-consistent merging and a multi-task merging approach using representation similarity. Provides comprehensive foundations for the model merging field.

entry.title: SplitZip: Ultra Fast Lossless KV Compression for Disaggregated LLM Serving

author.name: Yipin Guo, Siddharth Joshi

entry.summary: SplitZip proposes ultra-fast lossless KV cache compression for disaggregated LLM serving, addressing the bottleneck of transferring KV caches between prefill and decode workers. Designed specifically for the prefill-decode disaggregation paradigm in modern LLM serving systems. Targets long-input and agentic workloads.

entry.title: Talk is Cheap, Communication is Hard: Dynamic Grounding Failures and Repair in Multi-Agent Negotiation

author.name: Yiheng Yao, Chelsea Zou, Robert D. Hawkins

entry.summary: Studies dynamic grounding failures in multi-agent LLM negotiations where agents must collaboratively establish shared meaning. Shows that while individual agents can identify Pareto-optimal allocations, agent dyads consistently fail to reach them in open negotiation. Highlights inability to repair grounding breakdowns across turns.

entry.title: RMGAP: Benchmarking the Generalization of Reward Models across Diverse Preferences

author.name: Yangyang Zhou, Yi-Chen Li

entry.summary: RMGAP benchmarks reward model generalizability across diverse user preferences, addressing the limitation that existing benchmarks assume universal preference. Generates four distinct response variations per task and evaluates whether reward models correctly rank responses aligned with diverse preferences across Chat, Writing, Reasoning, and Safety domains.

entry.title: STABLEVAL: Disagreement-Aware and Stable Evaluation of AI Systems

author.name: Akash Bonagiri, Gerard Janno Anderias, Saee Patil, Angelina Lai, Devang Borkar, Gezheng Kang, Ishant Gandhi, Setareh Rafatirad, Houman Homayoun

entry.summary: STABLEVAL introduces a disagreement-aware evaluation framework that models annotator reliability and item ambiguity to produce calibrated system scores, addressing instability in human evaluation of AI systems under majority vote aggregation.

entry.title: Boundary Mass and the Soft-to-Hard Limit in Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Reza Rastegar

entry.summary: Provides mathematical analysis of the soft-to-hard routing limit in mixture-of-experts models, proving that boundary mass (probability of routing ties) is linear in slab width and deriving quantitative risk bounds for the transition.

entry.title: When Attention Collapses: Residual Evidence Modeling for Compositional Inference

author.name: Niklas Houba

entry.summary: Identifies 'slot collapse' as a failure mode in attention-based compositional inference under additive superposition, where multiple slots converge to the same dominant component. Proposes residual evidence modeling as a solution.

entry.title: APIOT: Autonomous Vulnerability Management Across Bare-Metal Industrial OT Networks

author.name: Adel ElZemity, Budi Arief, Shujun Li, Calvin Brierley, Yichao Wang, Yuxiang Huang, James Pope, Haoxiang Li, George Oikonomou

entry.summary: APIOT presents the first LLM-based autonomous pentesting framework targeting bare-metal operational technology devices running Modbus/TCP and CoAP, demonstrating autonomous exploit reasoning at the protocol level.

entry.title: On the Invariants of Softmax Attention

author.name: Wonsuk Lee

entry.summary: Defines the 'energy field' (row-centered attention logits) in softmax attention and shows it exhibits invariant properties across models, architectures, and inputs. Identifies mechanism-level invariants (zero-sum, rank bounds) and model-level regularities (exponential tail decay).

entry.title: RouteHijack: Routing-Aware Attack on Mixture-of-Experts LLMs

author.name: Zhiyuan Xu, Joseph Gardiner, Sana Belguith, Lichao Wu

entry.summary: Presents RouteHijack, a routing-aware jailbreak attack for Mixture-of-Experts LLMs that exploits the observation that safety behavior is concentrated in specific experts, bypassing them through routing manipulation.

entry.title: The Right Answer, the Wrong Direction: Why Transformers Fail at Counting and How to Fix It

author.name: Gabriel Garcia

entry.summary: Demonstrates that transformers internally represent counts correctly (probes achieve R²>0.99) but fail at output because count-encoding directions are nearly orthogonal to digit token output head rows. Proposes fixes via output head projection.

entry.title: Two Calls, Two Moments, and the Vote-Accuracy Curve of Repeated LLM Inference

author.name: Yi Liu

entry.summary: Analyzes repeated LLM inference under majority voting, showing that two labeled calls suffice to identify the mean and second moment of latent success probability, yielding sharp distribution-free bounds on vote accuracy curves.

entry.title: GRIFDIR: Graph Resolution-Invariant FEM Diffusion Models in Function Spaces over Irregular Domains

author.name: James Rowbottom, Elizabeth L. Baker, Nick Huang, Ben Adcock, Carola-Bibiane Sch\"onlieb, Alexander Denker

entry.summary: Proposes GRIFDIR, a function-space diffusion model architecture using graph convolutional kernels represented as finite element functions, enabling handling of unstructured meshes and complex geometries with resolution invariance.

entry.title: Most ReLU Networks Admit Identifiable Parameters

author.name: Moritz Grillo, Guido Mont\'ufar

entry.summary: Proves that for most ReLU network architectures (width ≥ 2), there exists an open set of identifiable parameters, meaning functions determine parameters up to scaling and permutation. Establishes generic depth hierarchy.

entry.title: Nora: Normalized Orthogonal Row Alignment for Scalable Matrix Optimizer

author.name: Jinghui Yuan, Jiaxuan Zou, Shuo Wang, Yong Liu, Feiping Nie

entry.summary: Proposes Nora optimizer that achieves Muon-like preconditioning, scale-invariance stability, and computational efficiency through normalized orthogonal row alignment for LLM training.

entry.title: On Adaptivity in Zeroth-Order Optimization

author.name: Hassan Dbouk, Nidham Gazagnadou, Matthias Reisser, Christos Louizos

entry.summary: Shows adaptive ZO methods like ZO-Adam offer no convergence advantage over ZO-SGD for LLM fine-tuning due to lack of coordinate-wise heterogeneity in high dimensions. Proposes MEAZO with scalar adaptation.

entry.title: Provable Accuracy Collapse in Embedding-Based Representations under Dimensionality Mismatch

author.name: Dionysis Arvanitakis, Vaggos Chatziafratis, Yiyuan Luo

entry.summary: Proves sharp dimension-accuracy tradeoffs for embedding representations, showing that unless embedding dimension d is chosen close to ground-truth dimension D, accuracy undergoes sudden collapse. Demonstrates this in contrastive learning with triplet supervision.

entry.title: MEMSAD: Gradient-Coupled Anomaly Detection for Memory Poisoning in Retrieval-Augmented Agents

author.name: Ishrith Gowda (University of California, Berkeley)

entry.summary: Formalizes memory poisoning attacks on retrieval-augmented agents as a Stackelberg game, proposes MEMSAD defense based on gradient coupling theorem. Shows faithful evaluation increases measured attack success by 4x, highlighting protocol issues in prior work.

entry.title: Agentic-imodels: Evolving agentic interpretability tools via autoresearch

author.name: Chandan Singh, Yan Shuo Tan, Weijia Xu, Zelalem Gero, Weiwei Yang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao

entry.summary: Introduces Agentic-imodels, an autoresearch loop that evolves scikit-learn-compatible regressors optimized for both predictive performance and LLM-based interpretability metrics. Proposes tools designed to be interpretable by agents rather than humans.

entry.title: A framework for analyzing concept representations in neural models

author.name: Burin Naowarat, Hao Tang, Sharon Goldwater

entry.summary: Introduces a unified framework to study concept representations in neural models along two axes: containment and disentanglement. Compares five concept subspace estimators across text and speech models, highlighting non-uniqueness issues.

entry.title: Beyond Perplexity: Character Distribution Signatures and the MDTA Benchmark for AI Text Detection

author.name: Priyadarshan Narayanasamy, Swastik Agrawal, Klint Faber, Fardina Fathmiul Alam

entry.summary: Introduces character distribution signatures as a training-free AI text detection signal, arguing that AI models approximate global character patterns while humans exhibit domain-specialized distributions. Constructs MDTA benchmark.

entry.title: StressEval: Failure-Driven Dynamic Benchmarking for Knowledge-Intensive Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Yongrui Chen, Yangyang Ma, Xiaoying Huang, Shenyu Zhang, Huajun Chen, Haofen Wang, Guilin Qi

entry.summary: Proposes StressEval, a failure-driven dynamic benchmark framework that generates challenging test instances from observed model failures, addressing contamination and staleness in static benchmarks.

entry.title: Decoding-Time Debiasing via Process Reward Models: From Controlled Fill-in to Open-Ended Generation

author.name: Muneeb Ur Raheem Khan

entry.summary: Proposes Process Reward Models for decoding-time debiasing of LLMs, scoring candidate tokens for fairness and fluency without modifying model weights. Designs three schemes of increasing sophistication.

entry.title: Flexi-LoRA with Input-Adaptive Ranks: Efficient Finetuning for Speech and Reasoning Tasks

author.name: Zongqian Li, Yixuan Su, Han Zhou, Zihao Fu, Nigel Collier

entry.summary: Presents Flexi-LoRA, dynamically adjusting LoRA ranks based on input complexity during training and inference. Shows consistency between training/inference dynamics is important for sequential reasoning tasks.

entry.title: AniMatrix: An Anime Video Generation Model that Thinks in Art, Not Physics

author.name: Tencent HY Team

entry.summary: Presents AniMatrix from Tencent, a video generation model for anime that replaces physical correctness with artistic correctness through a Production Knowledge System encoding anime conventions and a dual-channel conditioning mechanism.

entry.title: Safety in Embodied AI: A Survey of Risks, Attacks, and Defenses

author.name: Xiao Li, Xiang Zheng, Yifeng Gao, Xinyu Xia, Yixu Wang, Xin Wang, Ye Sun, Yunhan Zhao, Ming Wen, Jiayu Li, Xun Gong, Yi Liu, Yige Li, Yutao Wu, Cong Wang, Jun Sun, Yixin Cao, Zhineng Chen, Jingjing Chen, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Zuxuan Wu, Xipeng Qiu, Xuanjing Huang, Tiehua Zhang, Zhipeng Wei, Hanxun Huang, Sarah Erfani, James Bailey, Jianping Wang, Wei-Ying Ma, Bo Li, Xingjun Ma, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: Comprehensive survey of safety in embodied AI covering risks, attacks, and defenses across the full pipeline from perception to action in safety-critical physical environments.

entry.title: RoboAlign-R1: Distilled Multimodal Reward Alignment for Robot Video World Models

author.name: Hao Wu, Yuqi Li, Yuan Gao, Fan Xu, Fan Zhang, Kun Wang, Penghao Zhao, Qiufeng Wang, Yizhou Zhao, Weiyan Wang, Yingli Tian, Xian Wu, Xiaomeng Huang

entry.summary: RoboAlign-R1 combines reward-aligned post-training with stabilized long-horizon inference for robot video world models. Introduces RobotWorldBench (10K annotated pairs) and a multimodal judge for six-dimensional evaluation of generated robot videos.

entry.title: Dawn of the "national security" tier of AI

author.name: Mitchell_Porter

entry.summary: Discusses the emerging 'national security' tier of AI following reports that the White House may require vetting of AI models before release, prompted by Claude Mythos's hacking capabilities. Speculates about nationalization implications.

entry.title: Steer Like the LLM: Activation Steering that Mimics Prompting

author.name: Geert Heyman, Frederik Vandeputte

entry.summary: Proposes that prompt steering can be viewed as activation steering, and introduces Prompt Steering Replacement (PSR) models that estimate token-specific steering coefficients. Shows popular activation steering methods are not faithful to prompt steering mechanics.

entry.title: Beyond Semantic Relevance: Counterfactual Risk Minimization for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Peiyang Liu, Qiang Yan, Ziqiang Cui, Di Liang, Xi Wang, Wei Ye

entry.summary: Proposes CoRM-RAG using counterfactual risk minimization to align retrieval with decision safety rather than mere semantic similarity. Addresses the 'Relevance-Robustness Gap' where relevance-maximizing retrieval reinforces user cognitive biases.

entry.title: The grip of grammar on meaning uncertainty: cross-linguistic evidence, neural correlates, and clinical relevance

author.name: Rui He, Claudio Palominos, Samuele Vallisa, Ni Yang, Han Zhang, Miguel \'Angel Santos Santos, Neguine Rezaii, Sergi Valero, Yonghua Huang, Huan Li, Hong Jiang, Yongjun Peng, Maria Francisca Alonso-S\'anchez, Frederike Stein, Tilo Kircher, Philipp Homan, Iris Sommer, Lena Palaniyappan, Wolfram Hinzen

entry.summary: Studies how grammar compresses meaning uncertainty across 20 languages, with fMRI correlates showing surprisal reduction tracked by brain activation. Finds selective disruption in disorders, linking linguistics to clinical neuroscience.

entry.title: SRTJ: Self-Evolving Rule-Driven Training-Free LLM Jailbreaking

author.name: Jindong Li, Ying Liu, Yali Fu, Jinjing Zhu, Leyao Wang, Menglin Yang, Rex Ying

entry.summary: Proposes SRTJ, a self-evolving rule-driven training-free jailbreaking method that systematically accumulates and composes reusable attack rules from both successes and failures.

entry.title: MIRL: Mutual Information-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yin Zhang, Jiaxuan Zhao, Zonghan Wu, Zengxiang Li, Junfeng Fang, Kun Wang, Qingsong Wen, Yilei Shao

entry.summary: Introduces MIRL, using mutual information between generated descriptions and ground truth to guide RL for vision-language models, addressing visual perception errors that waste sampling budget.

entry.title: Effect-Transparent Governance for AI Workflow Architectures: Semantic Preservation, Expressive Minimality, and Decidability Boundaries

author.name: Alan L. McCann

entry.summary: Provides a machine-checked formal verification (in Rocq/Coq) that governance can be imposed on AI workflows without reducing computational expressivity. Proves 454 theorems across 36 modules demonstrating that effect-level governance is compatible with Turing completeness.

entry.title: Lifting Traces to Logic: Programmatic Skill Induction with Neuro-Symbolic Learning for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks

author.name: Jie-Jing Shao, Haiyan Yin, Yueming Lyu, Xingrui Yu, Lan-Zhe Guo, Ivor Tsang, James Kwok, Yu-Feng Li

entry.summary: Proposes Neuro-Symbolic Skill Induction (NSI) that lifts agent interaction traces into modular logic-grounded programs with explicit control flows and variable binding, enabling few-shot skill generalization.

entry.title: Evaluating Agentic AI in the Wild: Failure Modes, Drift Patterns, and a Production Evaluation Framework

author.name: Mukund Pandey

entry.summary: Presents a taxonomy of seven failure modes unique to production agentic AI systems and proposes an evaluation framework addressing compounding errors, tool failure cascades, and output drift in billion-event scale systems.

entry.title: Neural Decision-Propagation for Answer Set Programming

author.name: Thomas Eiter, Katsumi Inoue, Sota Moriyama

entry.summary: Proposes Neural Decision-Propagation (NDProp), a differentiable method for computing answer set programming stable models without classical solvers, using neural decisions and fuzzy propagations.

entry.title: Anon: Extrapolating Optimizer Adaptivity Across the Real Spectrum

author.name: Yiheng Zhang, Kaiyan Zhao, Shaowu Wu, Yiming Wang, Jiajun Wu, Leong Hou U, Steve Drew, Xiaoguang Niu

entry.summary: Proposes Anon optimizer with continuously tunable adaptivity across the real spectrum, interpolating between SGD-like and Adam-like behaviors. Introduces convergence guarantees across the entire adaptivity range.

entry.title: HeavySkill: Heavy Thinking as the Inner Skill in Agentic Harness

author.name: Jianing Wang, Linsen Guo, Zhengyu Chen, Qi Guo, Hongyu Zang, Wenjie Shi, Haoxiang Ma, Xiangyu Xi, Xiaoyu Li, Wei Wang, Xunliang Cai

entry.summary: Proposes HeavySkill, identifying 'heavy thinking' as a key inner skill in agentic frameworks that follows a two-stage pipeline of parallel reasoning then summarization. Provides systematic empirical study showing this skill drives performance beneath complex orchestration systems.

entry.title: Hybrid Inspection and Task-Based Access Control in Zero-Trust Agentic AI

author.name: Majed El Helou, Benjamin Ryder, Chiara Troiani, Jean Diaconu, Herv\'e Muyal, Marcelo Yannuzzi

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid runtime enforcement model for authorizing LLM agents that combines inspection of tool calls with task-based access control in zero-trust architectures. Addresses security risks of multi-agent collaboration with dynamic tool invocation.

entry.title: H-Probes: Extracting Hierarchical Structures From Latent Representations of Language Models

author.name: Cutter Dawes, Aryan Sharma, Angelos Ioannis Lagos, Shivam Raval

entry.summary: Develops H-probes, linear probes that extract hierarchical structure (depth and pairwise distance) from LLM latent representations. Shows in synthetic tree traversal tasks that hierarchy-containing subspaces are necessary for task completion.

entry.title: When Less Is More: Simplicity Beats Complexity for Physics-Constrained InSAR Phase Unwrapping

author.name: Prabhjot Singh, Manmeet Singh

entry.summary: Demonstrates that a simple vanilla U-Net outperforms complex attention-based architectures for InSAR phase unwrapping, providing physical justification via power spectral density analysis. Conducts the first large-scale architectural ablation on a global LiCSAR benchmark.

entry.title: LEAP: Layer-wise Exit-Aware Pretraining for Efficient Transformer Inference

author.name: Shashank Kapadia, Deep Naryan Mishra, Sujal Reddy Alugubelli, Haoan Wang, Saipraveen Vabbilisetty, Rishi Bhatia, Anupriya Sharma

entry.summary: Introduces LEAP, a pretraining objective that reconciles layer-aligned distillation with early-exit inference by ensuring intermediate representations converge sufficiently for exit decisions. Requires no architectural modifications.

entry.title: The Productivity-Reliability Paradox: Specification-Driven Governance for AI-Augmented Software Development

author.name: Sabry E. Farrag

entry.summary: Identifies the Productivity-Reliability Paradox in AI-augmented software development through a multivocal literature review of 67 sources. Shows 98% more PRs but 91% longer review times, proposing specification-driven governance.

entry.title: MAD-OPD: Breaking the Ceiling in On-Policy Distillation via Multi-Agent Debate

author.name: Jianze Wang, Ying Liu, Jinlong Chen, Xuchun Hu, Qilong Zhang, Yu Cao, Jun Wang, Hua Yang, Yong Xie, Qianglong Chen

entry.summary: Proposes MAD-OPD, breaking the single-teacher capability ceiling in on-policy distillation by using multi-agent debate among teachers. Weighted contributions based on post-debate confidence create emergent collective intelligence.

entry.title: LiveFMBench: Unveiling the Power and Limits of Agentic Workflows in Specification Generation

author.name: Dong Xu, Jialun Cao, Guozhao Mo, Junjie Hu, Cheng Wen, Hongyu Lin, Xianpei Han, Shengchao Qin, Cong Tian, Shing-Chi Cheung, Le Sun, Yaojie Lu

entry.summary: LiveFMBench introduces a continuously evolving benchmark of 630 ACSL-annotated C programs for evaluating LLM-based formal specification generation, designed to mitigate data contamination. It systematically evaluates different prompting strategies, reasoning modes, and agentic workflows for this task. Addresses an important gap in understanding LLM capabilities for formal methods.

entry.title: Where Do Prompt Perturbations Break Generation? A Segment-Level View of Robustness in LoRA-Tuned Language Models

author.name: Zhuoyun Li, Boxuan Wang, Jinwei Hu, Zhenglin Huang, Qisong He, Xinmiao Huang, Guangliang Cheng, Xiaowei Huang, Yi Dong

entry.summary: S²R² introduces segment-level robustness analysis for LoRA fine-tuning, showing that prompt perturbations can cause critical drift in specific entities or conclusions even when global similarity is preserved. Uses optimal transport to align semantic segments between clean and perturbed generations. Adds adapter-stability regularization for targeted robustness.

entry.title: Prosa: Rubric-Based Evaluation of LLMs on Real User Chats in Brazilian Portuguese

author.name: Roseval Malaquias Junior, Giovana Kerche Bon\'as, Thales Sales Almeida, Hugo Abonizio, Thiago Laitz, Ramon Pires, Marcos Piau, Celio Larcher, Rodrigo Nogueira

entry.summary: Introduces Prosa, the first real-user multi-turn Brazilian Portuguese chat benchmark with rubric-based LLM evaluation. Shows that binary rubric scoring with multi-judge filtering removes judge model sensitivity that plagues holistic scoring - three judges agree on all 16 ranks vs only 7/16 with holistic scoring. Increases score gaps between models by 47%.

entry.title: SignVerse-2M: A Two-Million-Clip Pose-Native Universe of 25+ Sign Languages

author.name: Sen Fang, Hongbin Zhong, Yanxin Zhang, Dimitris N. Metaxas

entry.summary: SignVerse-2M presents a two-million-clip pose-native dataset spanning 25+ sign languages, designed for both recognition/translation and pose-driven video generation. Addresses the gap between RGB-based models (sensitive to recording conditions) and modern pose-guided generation frameworks. Provides unified keypoint representation across sign languages.

entry.title: Selector-Guided Autonomous Curriculum for One-Shot Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Rudray Dave, Vedang Dubey, Smit Deoghare, Sudhakar Mishra

entry.summary: Proposes Selector-Guided Autonomous Curriculum (SGAC) for one-shot RLVR that uses a learnable selector on multi-dimensional features instead of static reward variance heuristics for instance selection. Addresses that reward variance is misleading as a transferability measure. Improves math reasoning in LLMs with better instance selection.

entry.title: TRAP: Tail-aware Ranking Attack for World-Model Planning

author.name: Siyuan Duan, Ke Zhang, Xizhao Luo

entry.summary: TRAP introduces a tail-aware ranking attack for world model planning that exploits the long-tailed ranking structure of imagined trajectories. Shows that world models have a distinct backdoor vulnerability different from reactive models - the planning process can't simply wash out perturbations targeting ranking structure. First targeted attack exploiting world model planning.

entry.title: RamanBench: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Machine Learning on Raman Spectroscopy

author.name: Mario Koddenbrock, Christoph Lange, Robin Legner, Martin J\"ager, Martin K\"ogler, Mariano N. Cruz Bournazou, Peter Neubauer, Felix Biessmann, Erik Rodner

entry.summary: RamanBench introduces the first large-scale standardized benchmark for machine learning on Raman spectroscopy, unifying 74 datasets with 325,668 spectra across classification and regression tasks. This addresses a key gap in scientific ML where fragmented datasets and inconsistent evaluation have hindered progress.

entry.title: The Conversations Beneath the Code: Triadic Data for Long-Horizon Software Engineering Agents

author.name: Yelin Kim

entry.summary: Argues that the next generation of software engineering agents needs 'triadic data': synchronized human-human conversations, human-AI sessions, and multi-week cross-functional work context, rather than just code or solo-agent trajectories.

entry.title: Pretraining on Sleep Data Improves non-Sleep Biosignal Tasks

author.name: William Lehn-Schi{\o}ler, Magnus Ruud Kj{\ae}r, Phillip Hempel, Magnus Guldberg Pedersen, Rahul Thapa, Bryan He, Nicolai Spicher, Andreas Brink-Kjaer, Lars Kai Hansen, Emmanuel Mignot

entry.summary: Demonstrates that foundation models pretrained on sleep polysomnography data transfer effectively to non-sleep EEG and ECG tasks, outperforming training from scratch across eight downstream tasks.

entry.title: Set-Based Training of Neural Barrier Certificates for Safety Verification of Dynamical Systems

author.name: Miriam Kranzlm\"uller, Lukas Koller, Tobias Ladner, Matthias Althoff

entry.summary: Proposes set-based training of neural barrier certificates that integrates formal verification into the training loss, collapsing the iterative train-verify loop into a single optimization where zero loss proves safety.

entry.title: eOptShrinkQ: Near-Lossless KV Cache Compression Through Optimal Spectral Denoising and Quantization

author.name: Pei-Chun Su

entry.summary: Proposes eOptShrinkQ, a KV cache compression pipeline that decomposes key-value cache into low-rank shared context and full-rank per-token residual using optimal singular value shrinkage, then quantizes the residual. Leverages spiked random matrix model insights.

entry.title: OGPO: Sample Efficient Full-Finetuning of Generative Control Policies

author.name: Sarvesh Patil, Mitsuhiko Nakamoto, Manan Agarwal, Shashwat Saxena, Jesse Zhang, Giri Anantharaman, Cleah Winston, Chaoyi Pan, Douglas Chen, Nai-Chieh Huang, Zeynep Temel, Oliver Kroemer, Sergey Levine, Abhishek Gupta, Hongkai Da, Paarth Shah, Max Simchowitz

entry.summary: Introduces OGPO (Off-policy Generative Policy Optimization) for sample-efficient fine-tuning of generative control policies (diffusion/flow-based) using off-policy critics and modified PPO objectives. Achieves SOTA on manipulation tasks.

entry.title: Pairwise matrices for sparse autoencoders: single-feature inspection mislabels causal axes

author.name: Michael A. Riegler, Birk Sebastian Frostelid Torpmann-Hagen

entry.summary: Proposes pairwise matrix protocol for SAE interpretability that co-varies steering coefficient with joint conditions, revealing that single-feature inspection mislabels causal axes. Shows inverted U-shapes and non-additive interactions between features.

entry.title: Fully Automatic Trace Gas Plume Detection

author.name: V\'it R\r{u}\v{z}i\v{c}ka, David R. Thompson, Jay E. Fahlen, Amanda M. Lopez, Steven Lu, Chuchu Xiang, Holly Bender, Daniel Jensen, Philip G. Brodrick, Jake Lee, Brian Bue, Daniel H. Cusworth, Luis Guanter, Adam Chlus, Andrew Thorpe, Robert O. Green

entry.summary: Presents a fully automated framework combining ML-based morphological analysis with physics-based spectroscopic fitting to detect trace gas plumes from imaging spectrometer data without human participation. Applied to EMIT satellite data for environmental monitoring.

entry.title: Flow Matching on Symmetric Spaces

author.name: Francesco Ruscelli, Ferdinando Zanchetta, Rita Fioresi

entry.summary: Introduces flow matching on Riemannian symmetric spaces by reformulating it as flow matching on a Lie algebra subspace, linearizing geodesic handling. Demonstrated on real Grassmannians.

entry.title: Uni-OPD: Unifying On-Policy Distillation with a Dual-Perspective Recipe

author.name: Wenjin Hou, Shangpin Peng, Weinong Wang, Zheng Ruan, Yue Zhang, Zhenglin Zhou, Mingqi Gao, Yifei Chen, Kaiqi Wang, Hongming Yang, Chengquan Zhang, Zhuotao Tian, Han Hu, Yi Yang, Fei Wu, Hehe Fan

entry.summary: Proposes Uni-OPD, a unified on-policy distillation framework for LLMs and MLLMs that addresses insufficient exploration and unreliable teacher supervision through dual-perspective optimization.

entry.title: Flow Sampling: Learning to Sample from Unnormalized Densities via Denoising Conditional Processes

author.name: Aaron Havens, Brian Karrer, Neta Shaul

entry.summary: Introduces Flow Sampling, a framework for sampling from unnormalized densities using denoising conditional processes. Training objective regresses onto denoising diffusion drift constructed from energy function.

entry.title: CreativityBench: Evaluating Agent Creative Reasoning via Affordance-Based Tool Repurposing

author.name: Cheng Qian, Hyeonjeong Ha, Jiayu Liu, Bingxiang He, Jeonghwan Kim, Jiateng Liu, Bingxuan Li, Aditi Tiwari, Dwip Dalal, Zhenhailong Wang, Xiusi Chen, Mahdi Namazifar, Yunzhu Li, Heng Ji

entry.summary: Introduces CreativityBench evaluating LLM creative tool use through affordance-based reasoning. Builds a large-scale affordance knowledge base with 4K entities and 150K+ annotations, generating 14K grounded tasks.

entry.title: Geometric Deviation as an Unsupervised Pre-Generation Reliability Signal: Probing LLM Representations for Answerability

author.name: Yucheng Du

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLM representation geometry can serve as a pre-generation signal for detecting unanswerable queries, measuring hidden state deviation from an answerable reference set. Finds strong separation for math prompts (AUC 0.78-0.84) but geometry primarily encodes task form rather than universal answerability. Tests across Llama 3.1-8B, Qwen 2.5-7B, and Mistral-7B.

entry.title: Where Paths Split: Localized, Calibrated Control of Moral Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Chenchen Yuan, Zheyu Zhang, Gjergji Kasneci

entry.summary: Presents Convergent-Divergent Routing for inference-time steering of LLM moral reasoning, finding and editing minimal branch points where ethical framework pathways diverge. Uses Common Spatial Patterns to extract discriminative directions at branch-point layers.

entry.title: Tempered Guided Diffusion

author.name: Andreas Makris, Paul Fearnhead, Chris Nemeth

entry.summary: Proposes Tempered Guided Diffusion (TGD), an annealed sequential Monte Carlo framework for training-free conditional sampling with diffusion priors. Uses tempered posteriors with particle reweighting and resampling to improve computation allocation efficiency.

entry.title: Conditional Diffusion Sampling

author.name: Francisco M. Castro-Mac\'ias, Pablo Morales-\'Alvarez, Saifuddin Syed, Daniel Hern\'andez-Lobato, Rafael Molina, Jos\'e Miguel Hern\'andez-Lobato

entry.summary: Introduces Conditional Diffusion Sampling (CDS) combining Parallel Tempering with diffusion-based approaches via Conditional Interpolants - stochastic processes with exact closed-form SDEs requiring no neural approximation. Addresses multimodal unnormalized distribution sampling.

entry.title: Lost in the Tower of Babel: The Adverse Effects of Incidental Multilingualism in LLMs

author.name: Anjishnu Mukherjee, Chutong Meng, Antonios Anastasopoulos

entry.summary: Argues that LLM multilingualism is 'incidental' - arising from uneven web training data rather than intentional design. Shows systematic inequalities across languages with empirical study of language self-reporting vs. actual response behavior.

entry.title: On Stable Long-Form Generation: Benchmarking and Mitigating Length Volatility

author.name: Zhitao He, Haolin Yang, Rui Min, Zeyu Qin, Yi R. Fung

entry.summary: Introduces VOLTBench to systematically quantify length volatility in LLM long-form generation, probes attention mechanisms to identify causes, and proposes mitigation strategies. Addresses overlooked reliability issue in LLM outputs.

entry.title: Do Large Language Models Plan Answer Positions? Position Bias in Multiple-Choice Question Generation

author.name: Xuemei Tang, Xufeng Duan, Zhenguang G. Cai

entry.summary: Reveals systematic position biases in LLM-generated multiple-choice questions, showing hidden representations encode predictive signals of correct answer position, suggesting implicit answer position planning during generation.

entry.title: Learn-to-learn on Arbitrary Textual Conditioning: A Hypernetwork-Driven Meta-Gated LLM

author.name: Luo Ji, Qi Qin, Ningyuan Xi, Teng Chen, Qingqing Gu, Hongyan Li

entry.summary: Proposes a hypernetwork-driven meta-gating mechanism that dynamically adjusts the nonlinearity of FFN layers via the β parameter in SwiGLU blocks, conditioned on textual context for meta-controllability.

entry.title: Energy-Based Constraint Networks: Learning Structural Coherence Across Modalities

author.name: Chirag Shinde

entry.summary: Introduces energy-based constraint networks that learn structural coherence from contrastive pairs across modalities. Achieves 93.4% accuracy on trained corruption types and generalizes to unseen types in both text and vision.

entry.title: AHPA: Adaptive Hierarchical Prior Alignment for Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Ruibin Min, Yexin Liu, Aimin Pan, Changsheng Lu, Jiafei Wu, Kelu Yao, Xiaogang Xu, Harry Yang

entry.summary: Proposes AHPA (Adaptive Hierarchical Prior Alignment) for accelerating Diffusion Transformer training by adapting alignment granularity based on signal-to-noise ratio - coarse alignment in high-noise regimes and fine-grained in low-noise regimes.

entry.title: Mix3R: Mixing Feed-forward Reconstruction and Generative 3D Priors for Joint Multi-view Aligned 3D Reconstruction and Pose Estimation

author.name: Siyou Lin, Zhou Xue, Hongwen Zhang, Liang An, Dongping Li, Shaohui Jiao, Yebin Liu

entry.summary: Presents Mix3R, combining feed-forward reconstruction and generative 3D priors in a unified framework for joint multi-view 3D reconstruction and pose estimation, producing both coarse voxels and per-view point maps in an aligned manner.

entry.title: Audio-Visual Intelligence in Large Foundation Models

author.name: You Qin, Kai Liu, Shengqiong Wu, Kai Wang, Shijian Deng, Yapeng Tian, Junbin Xiao, Yazhou Xing, Yinghao Ma, Bobo Li, Roger Zimmermann, Lei Cui, Furu Wei, Jiebo Luo, Hao Fei

entry.summary: Comprehensive survey of Audio-Visual Intelligence in foundation models, covering understanding, generation, and reasoning across auditory and visual modalities, noting rapid industrial progress (Meta MovieGen, Google Veo-3).

entry.title: Information Theory and Statistical Learning

author.name: Abbas El Gamal

entry.summary: A chapter draft for the third edition of Cover and Thomas's 'Elements of Information Theory' covering the intersection of information theory and statistical learning, focusing on model training applications.

entry.title: TimeTok: Granularity-Controllable Time-Series Generation via Hierarchical Tokenization

author.name: Seokhyun Lee, Jaeho Kim, Changjun Oh, Mihaela van der Schaar, Changhee Lee

entry.summary: Introduces TimeTok, a framework for granularity-controllable time-series generation using hierarchical tokenization that maps time series into coarse-to-fine token sequences for autoregressive generation at any target granularity.

entry.title: CoFlow: Coordinated Few-Step Flow for Offline Multi-Agent Decision Making

author.name: Guowei Zou, Haitao Wang, Beiwen Zhang, Boning Zhang, Hejun Wu

entry.summary: Proposes CoFlow for offline multi-agent RL, combining Coordinated Velocity Attention with Adaptive Coordination Gating to enable single-pass multi-agent generation while preserving inter-agent coordination.

entry.title: SciResearcher: Scaling Deep Research Agents for Frontier Scientific Reasoning

author.name: Tianshi Zheng, Rui Wang, Xiyun Li, Yangqiu Song, Tianqing Fang

entry.summary: Introduces SciResearcher, an automated agentic framework for frontier scientific reasoning that scales deep research agents through specialized academic source retrieval and multi-step computational reasoning.

entry.title: Catching the Infection Before It Spreads: Foresight-Guided Defense in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yue Ma, Ziyuan Yang, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a foresight-guided defense against infectious jailbreak in multi-agent systems that addresses localized interaction behaviors rather than applying global cure factors, avoiding response homogenization.

entry.title: Retrieval and Multi-Hop Reasoning in 1M-Token Context Windows: Evaluating LLMs on Classical Chinese Text

author.name: Eric H. C. Chow

entry.summary: Evaluates five frontier LLMs with 1M-token context windows on classical Chinese retrieval and 3-hop reasoning, finding that single-needle retrieval succeeds but multi-hop reasoning degrades significantly at longer contexts.

entry.title: ANO: A Principled Approach to Robust Policy Optimization

author.name: Yiheng Zhang, Yiming Wang, Kaiyan Zhao, Zhenglin Wan, Jiayu Chen, Leong Hou U

entry.summary: Proposes Anchored Neighborhood Optimization (ANO) for robust policy optimization, deriving a Redescending Influence Principle that addresses PPO's clipping limitations. Establishes a Unified Trust Region Framework generalizing existing RL objectives.

entry.title: DataClaw: A Process-Oriented Agent Benchmark for Exploratory Real-World Data Analysis

author.name: Qiaohong Zhang, Weihao Ye, Jialong Chen, Yi Luo, BoYuan Li, Bowen Deng, Zibin Zheng, Jianhao Lin, Wei-Shi Zheng, Chuan Chen
