entry.summary: Odysseus scales VLM-based decision-making to 100+ turn games (Super Mario Land) using RL. Proposes an adapted PPO variant with lightweight modifications for long-horizon visually grounded interaction. From Princeton researchers (Chi Jin, Karthik Narasimhan, Danqi Chen).

entry.title: Escaping Mode Collapse in LLM Generation via Geometric Regulation

author.name: Xin Du, Kumiko Tanaka-Ishii

entry.summary: Reinterprets mode collapse in LLMs as geometric collapse in representation space and proposes Reinforced Mode Regulation (RMR), a lightweight online intervention that prevents the model's trajectory from becoming confined to low-dimensional regions.

entry.title: Minimizing Collateral Damage in Activation Steering

author.name: Tam Nguyen, Tu Anh Nguyen, Sina Alemohammad, Richard G. Baraniuk

entry.summary: Formalizes 'collateral damage' in activation steering of LLMs - unintended changes to non-target feature directions - and proposes a constrained optimization framework that minimizes expected squared collateral change while achieving steering goals.

entry.title: Training Non-Differentiable Networks via Optimal Transport

author.name: An T. Le

entry.summary: PolyStep is a gradient-free optimizer that trains non-differentiable neural networks (spiking neurons, quantized layers, discrete routing) using only forward passes. It evaluates loss at structured polytope vertices, computes softmax-weighted assignments, and displaces particles via barycentric projection derived from optimal transport theory.

entry.title: Reference-Sampled Boltzmann Projection for KL-Regularized RLVR: Target-Matched Weighted SFT, Finite One-Shot Gaps, and Policy Mirror Descent

author.name: Yao Shu, Chenxing Wei, Hongbin Lin, Shuang Qiu, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: Identifies the reference-sampled weighted-SFT objective whose induced policy equals the KL-regularized RLVR optimizer (Boltzmann target), connecting weighted SFT to online RLVR and characterizing finite one-shot gaps.

entry.title: The Cylindrical Representation Hypothesis for Language Model Steering

author.name: Lang Gao, Jinghui Zhang, Wei Liu, Fengxian Ji, Chenxi Wang, Zirui Song, Akash Ghosh, Youssef Mohamed, Preslav Nakov, Xiuying Chen

entry.summary: Proposes the Cylindrical Representation Hypothesis (CRH) as an extension of the Linear Representation Hypothesis for understanding model steering. CRH relaxes orthogonality assumptions while preserving linear representations, explaining why steering effects are often unstable and unpredictable through overlapping concept contributions and sample-specific axis-orthogonal structure.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems through Orchestration Traces

author.name: Chenchen Zhang

entry.summary: Studies reinforcement learning for LLM-based multi-agent systems through orchestration traces - temporal interaction graphs capturing spawning, delegation, communication, and aggregation. Identifies three technical axes: reward design, credit assignment, and signal attachment.

entry.title: Linear-Time Global Visual Modeling without Explicit Attention

author.name: Ruize He, Dongchen Han, Gao Huang

entry.summary: Demonstrates that attention can be reframed as an MLP with dynamically predicted parameters, then investigates whether linear-time global modeling can match Transformer performance without explicit attention computation. From Tsinghua (Gao Huang's group).

entry.title: Accurate Legal Reasoning at Scale: Neuro-Symbolic Offloading and Structural Auditability for Robust Legal Adjudication

author.name: Stanis{\l}aw S\'ojka, Witold Kowalczyk

entry.summary: Proposes Amortized Intelligence, a neuro-symbolic approach where an LLM translates legal text once into a typed graph representation (DACL), then adjudication uses deterministic graph execution with auditable traces. Achieves near-perfect consistency compared to GPT-5.2 and Gemini 3 Pro baselines.

entry.title: ContextualJailbreak: Evolutionary Red-Teaming via Simulated Conversational Priming

author.name: Mario Rodr\'iguez B\'ejar, Francisco J. Cort\'es-Delgado, S. Braghin, Jose L. Hern\'andez-Ramos

entry.summary: Proposes ContextualJailbreak, an evolutionary red-teaming approach that uses simulated conversational priming for multi-turn jailbreak attacks on LLMs. Automates the discovery of effective multi-turn attack strategies that exploit contextual priming.

entry.title: Measuring AI Reasoning: A Guide for Researchers

author.name: Munachiso Samuel Nwadike, Zangir Iklassov, Kareem Ali, Rifo Genadi, Kentaro Inui

entry.summary: Provides a guide for researchers on evaluating reasoning in language models, arguing that reasoning should be assessed through evidence of adaptive multi-step search rather than final-answer accuracy. Formalizes reasoning as a search-like procedure requiring variable-depth computation.

entry.title: Physically Native World Models: A Hamiltonian Perspective on Generative World Modeling

author.name: Sen Cui, Jingheng Ma

entry.summary: Proposes a Hamiltonian mechanics-based framework for world models, arguing that physically native structures (energy conservation, symplectic geometry) can unify 2D video-generative, 3D scene-centric, and JEPA-like latent models. Claims the bottleneck is physical reliability, not visual generation quality.

entry.title: Can Coding Agents Reproduce Findings in Computational Materials Science?

author.name: Ziyang Huang, Yi Cao, Ali K. Shargh, Jing Luo, Ruidong Mei, Mohd Zaki, Zhan Liu, Wyatt Bunstine, William Jurayj, Somdatta Goswami, Tyrel McQueen, Michael Shields, Jaafar El-Awady, Paulette Clancy, Benjamin Van Durme, Nicholas Andrews, William Walden, Daniel Khashabi

entry.summary: Introduces AutoMat, a benchmark for evaluating LLM coding agents' ability to reproduce claims from computational materials science, testing procedure recovery, toolchain navigation, and scientific claim verification.

entry.title: Linking spatial biology and clinical histology via Haiku

author.name: Yan Cui, Jacob S. Leiby, Wenhui Lei, Dokyoon Kim, Yanxiang Deng, Aaron T. Mayer, Zhenqin Wu, Alexandro E. Trevino, Zhi Huang

entry.summary: Presents Haiku, a tri-modal contrastive learning model trained on 26.7M spatial proteomics patches from 3,218 tissue sections, enabling cross-modal retrieval between immunofluorescence, H&E histology, and clinical metadata.

entry.title: From Flat Facts to Sharp Hallucinations: Detecting Stubborn Errors via Gradient Sensitivity

author.name: Yee Zhing Liew, Andrew Huey Ping Tan, Anwar P. P Abdul Majeed

entry.summary: Proposes Embedding-Perturbed Gradient Sensitivity (EPGS) for detecting 'stubborn hallucinations' in LLMs by measuring gradient magnitude spikes after input perturbation, based on the hypothesis that hallucinations sit in sharp minima.

entry.title: A Theory of Generalization in Deep Learning

author.name: Elon Litman, Gabe Guo

entry.summary: Presents a non-asymptotic generalization theory for deep learning based on NTK partitioning of output space into signal and noise channels, showing how SGD's drift-diffusion dynamics suppress memorization while signal accumulates, even when the kernel evolves O(1) (feature learning regime).

entry.title: AdamO: A Collapse-Suppressed Optimizer for Offline RL

author.name: Nan Qiao, Sheng Yue, Shuning Wang, Ju Ren

entry.summary: AdamO addresses Q-value collapse in offline RL by analyzing optimizer dynamics from a control-theoretic viewpoint. Shows that collapse can be triggered by optimizer dynamics themselves and derives necessary/sufficient stability conditions for Adam-based critic updates.

entry.title: Break the Block: Dynamic-size Reasoning Blocks for Diffusion Large Language Models via Monotonic Entropy Descent with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yan Jiang, Ruihong Qiu, Zi Huang

entry.summary: Proposes dynamic-size reasoning blocks for diffusion large language models via monotonic entropy descent with reinforcement learning, addressing the fixed-size block bottleneck in semi-autoregressive generation for reasoning tasks.

entry.title: The Compliance Gap: Why AI Systems Promise to Follow Process Instructions but Don't

author.name: Kwan Soo Shin

entry.summary: Identifies the 'Compliance Gap' where AI systems verbally agree to follow process instructions but behaviorally violate them. Proves this gap is structurally inevitable under RL that rewards text without observing behavior.

entry.title: Model Organisms Are Leaky: Perplexity Differencing Often Reveals Finetuning Objectives

author.name: Mohammed Abu Baker, Luca Baroni, Dan Wilhelm

entry.summary: Shows that finetuning objectives can be revealed from model organisms (finetuned LLMs) using simple perplexity differencing, as models overgeneralize finetuned behaviors beyond intended contexts.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Hidden-State Dynamics as a Signature of Internal Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Kotaro Furuya, Takahito Tanimura

entry.summary: Investigates hidden-state transitions across decoding steps and layers in large reasoning models, identifying a distinct spatiotemporal pattern where successful reasoning trajectories exhibit broad temporal dynamics with localized layer-wise concentration. Formalizes this as Spatiotemporal characteristics that distinguish genuine reasoning from mere verbosity.

entry.title: Bucketing the Good Apples: A Method for Diagnosing and Improving Causal Abstraction

author.name: Li Puyin, Jiyuan Tan, Ahmad Jabbar, Thomas Icard, Atticus Geiger

entry.summary: Presents a method for diagnosing causal abstraction interpretability by partitioning input space into well-interpreted and under-interpreted regions based on pairwise interchange-intervention behavior. Makes causal abstraction a diagnostic tool revealing where interpretations work and fail.

entry.title: Visual Implicit Autoregressive Modeling

author.name: Pengfei Jiang, Jixiang Luo, Luxi Lin, Zhaohong Huang, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: Introduces VIAR (Visual Implicit Autoregressive Modeling), a next-scale autoregressive generator using implicit equilibrium layers with Jacobian-Free Backpropagation, achieving FID 2.16 on ImageNet 256x256 with only 38.4% parameters of VAR.

entry.title: Why Do LLMs Struggle in Strategic Play? Broken Links Between Observations, Beliefs, and Actions

author.name: Jan Sobotka, Mustafa O. Karabag, Ufuk Topcu

entry.summary: Uncovers two gaps in LLM strategic decision-making: an observation-belief gap (models have more accurate internal beliefs than verbal reports) and a belief-action gap (accurate beliefs don't reliably translate to optimal actions). Tests on Llama 3.1, Qwen3, and GPT-OSS.

entry.title: GAZE: Grounded Agentic Zero-shot Evaluation with Viewer-Level Tools and Literature Retrieval on Rare Brain MRI

author.name: Duaa Alim, Mogtaba Alim, Liam Chalcroft

entry.summary: Introduces GAZE, a framework enabling medical VLMs to work iteratively like radiologists by calling viewer-level tools and literature retrieval, achieving 58.2% accuracy on 906 rare brain MRI cases covering 281 conditions.

entry.title: Enhanced LLM Reasoning by Optimizing Reward Functions with Search-Driven Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Arash Ahmadi (Mike), Sarah Sharif (Mike), Yaser (Mike), Banad

entry.summary: Introduces a search-driven framework that treats reward function specification as an object of optimization for improving LLM mathematical reasoning. Candidate reward functions are generated by a frontier LLM, validated automatically, and screened through short GRPO training runs on Llama-3.

entry.title: Models Recall What They Violate: Constraint Adherence in Multi-Turn LLM Ideation

author.name: Garvin Kruthof

entry.summary: DriftBench evaluates constraint adherence in multi-turn LLM-assisted scientific ideation. Finds that models accurately restate constraints they simultaneously violate - a 'knows-but-violates' dissociation between declarative recall and behavioral adherence across 2,146 runs.

entry.title: AdaMeZO: Adam-style Zeroth-Order Optimizer for LLM Fine-tuning Without Maintaining the Moments

author.name: Zhijie Cai, Haolong Chen, Guangxu Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes AdaMeZO, a zeroth-order optimizer for LLM fine-tuning that achieves Adam-like adaptive learning without storing first and second moment estimates, maintaining the memory efficiency of MeZO.

entry.title: Probe-Geometry Alignment: Erasing the Cross-Sequence Memorization Signature Below Chance

author.name: Anamika Paul Rupa, Anietie Andy

entry.summary: Shows that memorization signatures from LLM unlearning are causally separable from recall capability via probes, and demonstrates surgical removal of these traces without measurable capability cost across multiple model scales.

entry.title: Efficient Preference Poisoning Attack on Offline RLHF

author.name: Chenye Yang, Weiyu Xu, Lifeng Lai

entry.summary: Studies label flip attacks against DPO, showing that flipping one preference label induces a parameter-independent gradient shift. Develops two attack methods (BAL-A and BMP-A) converting targeted poisoning into a structured binary sparse approximation problem.

entry.title: The Compliance Trap: How Structural Constraints Degrade Frontier AI Metacognition Under Adversarial Pressure

author.name: Rahul Kumar

entry.summary: SCHEMA evaluates metacognitive stability of 11 frontier models under adversarial pressure, finding 8/11 suffer catastrophic metacognitive degradation (up to 30.2pp accuracy drop) - a failure mode distinct from intentional deception.

entry.title: StressEval: Failure-Driven Dynamic Benchmarking for Knowledge-Intensive Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Yongrui Chen, Yangyang Ma, Xiaoying Huang, Shenyu Zhang, Huajun Chen, Haofen Wang, Guilin Qi

entry.summary: Proposes StressEval, a dynamic benchmarking framework that turns observed model failures into challenging test instances through a three-stage process: constructing difficulty cards, dual-perspective instance synthesis targeting knowledge gaps and reasoning breakdowns, and controllable difficulty generation.

entry.title: GR-Ben: A General Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Process Reward Models

author.name: Zhouhao Sun, Xuan Zhang, Xiao Ding, Bibo Cai, Li Du, Kai Xiong, Xinran Dai, Fei Zhang, weidi tang, Zhiyuan Kan, Yang Zhao, Bing Qin, Ting Liu

entry.summary: Introduces GR-Ben, a process-level benchmark for evaluating Process Reward Models across science and logic domains with nine subdomains. Addresses the limitation that existing PRM benchmarks focus only on mathematical reasoning.

entry.title: Are Tools All We Need? Unveiling the Tool-Use Tax in LLM Agents

author.name: Kaituo Zhang, Zhen Xiong, Mingyu Zhong, Zhimeng Jiang, Zhouyuan Yuan, Zhecheng Li, Ying Lin

entry.summary: Demonstrates that tool-augmented reasoning doesn't always outperform native chain-of-thought, especially with semantic distractors. Proposes a Factorized Intervention Framework isolating the 'tool-use tax' - performance degradation from the tool-calling protocol itself. Offers practical insights for when tools help vs. hurt.

entry.title: Mean-Field Path-Integral Diffusion: From Samples to Interacting Agents

author.name: Michael Chertkov

entry.summary: Introduces Mean-Field Path-Integral Diffusion (MF-PID), where diffusion model samples become interacting agents whose drift depends on the evolving population density. Unifies generative modeling and multi-agent control under Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman/Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck duality.

entry.title: Silicon Showdown: Performance, Efficiency, and Ecosystem Barriers in Consumer-Grade LLM Inference

author.name: Abdurrahman Javat, Allan Kazakov

entry.summary: Presents systematic empirical analysis comparing Nvidia Blackwell and Apple Silicon for consumer-grade LLM inference at 70B+ parameters, identifying a 'Backend Dichotomy' in TensorRT-LLM and characterizing architecture-specific tradeoffs.

entry.title: Structure Liberates: How Constrained Sensemaking Produces More Novel Research Output

author.name: James Mooney, Zae Myung Kim, Young-Jun Lee, Dongyeop Kang

entry.summary: Introduces SCISENSE, a sensemaking framework that operationalizes scientific ideation as 8 cognitive stages, creating 100K-scale datasets of research trajectories and distilling sensemaking LLMs that produce more novel research output.

entry.title: Persistent Visual Memory: Sustaining Perception for Deep Generation in LVLMs

author.name: Siyuan Huang, Xiaoye Qu, Yafu Li, Tong Zhu, Zefeng He, Muxin Fu, Daizong Liu, Wei-Long Zheng, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes Persistent Visual Memory (PVM), a learnable module addressing 'Visual Signal Dilution' in autoregressive LVLMs where visual attention decays as textual history grows, providing distance-agnostic visual retrieval.

entry.title: Learning in the Fisher Subspace: A Guided Initialization for LoRA Fine-Tuning

author.name: Zhi-Quan Feng, Ying-Jia Lin, Hung-Yu Kao

entry.summary: Proposes Fisher Information-guided LoRA initialization that identifies task-relevant subspaces using the Fisher information matrix, choosing directions that matter for the downstream data distribution rather than relying on weight geometry alone.

entry.title: When Less is Enough: Efficient Inference via Collaborative Reasoning

author.name: Yilei Chen, Sharut Gupta, Yannis Paschalidis, Ayush Sekhari, Aldo Pacchiano

entry.summary: Proposes DUET, a collaborative inference framework where a capable model produces reasoning signals and a lightweight model generates final answers, reducing inference costs while maintaining performance. Uses length-penalized joint optimization.

entry.title: Concepts Whisper While Syntax Shouts: Spectral Anti-Concentration and the Dual Geometry of Transformer Representations

author.name: Pratyush Acharya, Nuraj Rimal, Habish Dhakal

entry.summary: Discovers spectral anti-concentration in transformer residual streams across 17 models: concept directions concentrate in the spectral tail while syntax directions align with top singular vectors, revealing a dual geometry where 'concepts whisper while syntax shouts'.

entry.title: TRAP: Tail-aware Ranking Attack for World-Model Planning

author.name: Siyuan Duan, Ke Zhang, Xizhao Luo

entry.summary: TRAP identifies a novel backdoor vulnerability in world models for planning, rooted in the long-tailed ranking structure of imagined trajectories. Shows that existing shallow perturbation attacks are ineffective against world models' dynamics priors, but tail-aware ranking attacks can exploit trajectory evaluation.

entry.title: Generalized Distributional Alignment Games for Unbiased Answer-Level Fine-Tuning

author.name: Mehryar Mohri, Jon Schneider, Yutao Zhong

entry.summary: Generalizes the Distributional Alignment Game framework to arbitrary Bregman divergences, resolving systematic estimation bias from Jensen's inequality in standard algorithms. For polynomial rewards, constructs provably exact unbiased estimators using U-statistics.

entry.title: Visual Latents Know More Than They Say: Unsilencing Latent Reasoning in MLLMs

author.name: Xin Zhang, Qiqi Tao, Jiawei Du, Moyun Liu, Joey Tianyi Zhou

entry.summary: Identifies a previously overlooked optimization pathology in multimodal models where visual latent reasoning tokens become semantically enriched during training but their contribution to predictions is systematically suppressed ('Silenced Visual Latents'). The autoregressive objective creates shortcuts that bypass latent reasoning.

entry.title: Compared to What? Baselines and Metrics for Counterfactual Prompting

author.name: Zihao Yang, Mosh Levy, Yoav Goldberg, Byron C. Wallace

entry.summary: Argues that counterfactual prompting studies (measuring bias, CoT faithfulness) are methodologically flawed because they don't account for baseline model sensitivity to meaning-preserving paraphrases. Shows that gender-flip effects in MedQA are indistinguishable from simple paraphrasing effects.

entry.title: The Case for ESM3 as a General-Purpose AI Model with Systemic Risk Under the EU AI Act

author.name: Taro Qureshi, Jacob Griffith, Koen Holtman, Marcel Mir Teijeiro, Ze Shen Chin, Rokas Gipi\v{s}kis

entry.summary: Examines whether ESM3, a frontier biological foundation model, should be regulated under the EU AI Act as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk. Concludes it currently falls outside meaningful regulation and proposes remedial amendments.

entry.title: On Training Large Language Models for Long-Horizon Tasks: An Empirical Study of Horizon Length

author.name: Sunghwan Kim, Junhee Cho, Beong-woo Kwak, Taeyoon Kwon, Liang Wang, Nan Yang, Xingxing Zhang, Furu Wei, Jinyoung Yeo

entry.summary: Systematically studies how task horizon length affects LLM agent training dynamics, revealing that longer horizons alone create training bottlenecks that induce distinct failure modes even when decision rules remain identical.

entry.title: RMGAP: Benchmarking the Generalization of Reward Models across Diverse Preferences

author.name: Yangyang Zhou, Yi-Chen Li

entry.summary: Introduces RMGAP, a benchmark for evaluating reward model generalizability across diverse user preferences rather than a single universal preference. The benchmark includes 1,097 instances across Chat, Writing, Reasoning, and Safety domains with multiple preference-variant responses. This addresses a gap in how reward models are evaluated for RLHF alignment.

entry.title: SRTJ: Self-Evolving Rule-Driven Training-Free LLM Jailbreaking

author.name: Jindong Li, Ying Liu, Yali Fu, Jinjing Zhu, Leyao Wang, Menglin Yang, Rex Ying

entry.summary: Proposes SRTJ, a self-evolving rule-driven training-free jailbreaking method that systematically utilizes both successful and failed attack experiences. Includes mechanisms for composing and selecting reusable attack rules across different targets.

entry.title: SciResearcher: Scaling Deep Research Agents for Frontier Scientific Reasoning

author.name: Tianshi Zheng, Rui Wang, Xiyun Li, Yangqiu Song, Tianqing Fang

entry.summary: Introduces SciResearcher, an agentic framework for frontier scientific reasoning that addresses limitations of existing deep research agents when dealing with sparse academic sources and complex domain-specific reasoning.

entry.title: A Language for Describing Agentic LLM Contexts

author.name: Noga Peleg Pelc, Gal A. Kaminka, Yoav Goldberg

entry.summary: Proposes a formal language for describing agentic LLM contexts - how prompts are composed and evolve across interaction steps in LLM agent systems. Addresses the lack of standards for communicating context engineering decisions.

entry.title: Mamoda2.5: Enhancing Unified Multimodal Model with DiT-MoE

author.name: Yangming Shi, Shixiang Zhu, Tao Shen, Zhimiao Yu, Dengsheng Chen, Taicai Chen, Yunfei Yang, Juan Zhou, Chen Cheng, Liang Ma, Xibin Wu, Benxuan Yan, Ge Li, Tuoyu Zhang, Dan Li, Chang Liu, Zhenbang Sun

entry.summary: Mamoda2.5 presents a unified AR-Diffusion framework combining multimodal understanding and generation with a fine-grained MoE design (128 experts, Top-8 routing) in 25B parameters activating only 3B. Achieves top performance on VBench 2.0 and sets new records in video editing quality.

entry.title: MolmoAct2: Action Reasoning Models for Real-world Deployment

author.name: Haoquan Fang, Jiafei Duan, Donovan Clay, Sam Wang, Shuo Liu, Weikai Huang, Xiang Fan, Wei-Chuan Tsai, Shirui Chen, Yi Ru Wang, Shanli Xing, Jaemin Cho, Jae Sung Park, Ainaz Eftekhar, Peter Sushko, Karen Farley, Angad Wadhwa, Cole Harrison, Winson Han, Ying-Chun Lee, Eli VanderBilt, Rose Hendrix, Suveen Ellawela, Lucas Ngoo, Joyce Chai, Zhongzheng Ren, Ali Farhadi, Dieter Fox, Ranjay Krishna

entry.summary: Presents MolmoAct2, a fully open action reasoning model for practical robotic deployment. Introduces MolmoER VLM backbone trained on 3.3M samples, three new datasets, and advances along five axes over its predecessor.

entry.title: Thinking in Text and Images: Interleaved Vision--Language Reasoning Traces for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation

author.name: Jinkun Liu, Haohan Chi, Lingfeng Zhang, Yifan Xie, YuAn Wang, Long Chen, Hangjun Ye, Xiaoshuai Hao, Wenbo Ding

entry.summary: Introduces Interleaved Vision-Language Reasoning (IVLR), a policy framework for long-horizon robot manipulation that alternates textual subgoals with visual keyframes. A single multimodal transformer generates this semantic-geometric trace from initial observation, combining logical coherence with geometric grounding.

entry.title: Attention Is Where You Attack

author.name: Aviral Srivastava, Sourav Panda

entry.summary: Introduces the Attention Redistribution Attack (ARA), a white-box adversarial attack that identifies safety-critical attention heads and redirects attention away from safety-relevant positions. Bypasses safety alignment with as few as 5 adversarial tokens across LLaMA-3, Mistral, Gemma.

entry.title: LLM-Oriented Information Retrieval: A Denoising-First Perspective

author.name: Lu Dai, Liang Sun, Fanpu Cao, Ziyang Rao, Cehao Yang, Hao Liu, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: Argues that information retrieval should shift to a denoising-first paradigm for LLM consumption, proposing a four-stage framework addressing how noise in retrieved context directly causes hallucinations and reasoning failures in RAG systems.

entry.title: Make Your LVLM KV Cache More Lightweight

author.name: Xihao Chen, Yangyang Guo, Roger Zimmermann

entry.summary: Proposes LightKV, which reduces KV cache size in vision-language models by exploiting redundancy among vision tokens through prompt-aware cross-modality message passing and progressive compression during prefill.

entry.title: A Theory of Saddle Escape in Deep Nonlinear Networks

author.name: Divit Rawal, Michael R. DeWeese

entry.summary: Derives an exact identity for weight matrix norm imbalance in deep nonlinear networks, classifying activations into four universality classes, and obtains a critical-depth escape time law for saddle point escape during training.

entry.title: The Partial Testimony of Logs: Evaluation of Language Model Generation under Confounded Model Choice

author.name: Jikai Jin, Vasilis Syrgkanis

entry.summary: Studies offline evaluation of language models from confounded usage logs, proving an identification theorem that combines observational data, small randomized experiments, and offline simulators to obtain unbiased estimates of model quality.

entry.title: Adaptive Pluralistic Alignment: A pipeline for dynamic artificial democracy

author.name: Rachel Freedman

entry.summary: Proposes Adaptive Pluralistic Alignment (APA), a modular pipeline for updating AI alignment to track evolving societal values using low-rank reward basis decomposition, social-choice voting, and efficient adaptation without retraining.

entry.title: Projection-Free Transformers via Gaussian Kernel Attention

author.name: Debarshi Kundu, Archisman Ghosh, Swaroop Ghosh, Vasant Honavar

entry.summary: Introduces Gaussian Kernel Attention (GKA) that replaces learned Q/K/V projections with direct Gaussian RBF kernel similarity computation on per-head token features, requiring only a bandwidth parameter per head plus a single output projection.

entry.title: LLM Ghostbusters: Surgical Hallucination Suppression via Adaptive Unlearning

author.name: Joseph Spracklen, Pedram Aghazadeh, Farinaz Koushanfar, Murtuza Jadliwala

entry.summary: Proposes adaptive unlearning to suppress LLM hallucinations of non-existent software packages (slopsquatting), a supply-chain vulnerability where attackers register hallucinated packages with malicious payloads. Uses surgical unlearning to remove specific hallucinations without degrading utility.

entry.title: Hallucinations Undermine Trust; Metacognition is a Way Forward

author.name: Gal Yona, Mor Geva, Yossi Matias

entry.summary: Argues that hallucination reduction has come mainly from expanding knowledge boundaries rather than improving boundary awareness, and proposes metacognition as a path forward with analysis of calibration challenges.

entry.title: FlexSQL: Flexible Exploration and Execution Make Better Text-to-SQL Agents

author.name: Quang Hieu Pham, Yang He, Ping Nie, Canwen Xu, Davood Rafiei, Yuepeng Wang, Xi Ye, Jocelyn Qiaochu Chen

entry.summary: Presents FlexSQL, a text-to-SQL agent whose core principle is flexible database interaction - allowing schema exploration, data inspection, and verification at any point during reasoning. Generates diverse execution plans and uses two-tiered repair mechanisms.

entry.title: MIRL: Mutual Information-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yin Zhang, Jiaxuan Zhao, Zonghan Wu, Zengxiang Li, Junfeng Fang, Kun Wang, Qingsong Wen, Yilei Shao

entry.summary: Proposes MIRL, a mutual information-guided RL framework for Vision-Language Models that addresses visual perception errors by decoupling visual description from reasoning stages. Uses MI between descriptions and ground truth to provide stage-specific rewards.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Confidence Estimation for Small LLMs: When Supervised Baselines Aren't Worth Training

author.name: Luong N. Nguyen

entry.summary: Shows that average token log-probability, requiring no training data, matches or exceeds supervised RouteLLM-style baselines for confidence estimation in small (7-8B) language models. Demonstrates viability of zero-shot routing for local-to-cloud inference.

entry.title: X2SAM: Any Segmentation in Images and Videos

author.name: Hao Wang, Limeng Qiao, Chi Zhang, Lin Ma, Guanglu Wan, Xiangyuan Lan, Xiaodan Liang

entry.summary: Introduces X2SAM, a unified segmentation model that extends capabilities from images to videos, supporting both textual and visual prompts in one interface by coupling an LLM with a SAM-based segmentation module.

entry.title: OmniEncoder: See, Hear, and Feel Continuous Motion Like Humans With One Encoder

author.name: Detao Bai, Shimin Yao, Weixuan Chen, Chengen Lai, Yuanming Li, Zhiheng Ma, Xihan Wei

entry.summary: Presents OmniEncoder, a unified Transformer backbone that co-embeds visual and audio signals at symmetric 25fps, addressing the 'video-coarse, audio-dense' design limitation of current omni-modal LLMs that process modalities at different rates.

entry.title: Auto-review of agent actions without synchronous human oversight

author.name: papetoast

entry.summary: OpenAI describes their Auto-review system for Codex agents that replaces human approval with agent review at sandbox boundaries. Sessions stop for human approval 200x less often while still catching most dangerous actions.

entry.title: AEM: Adaptive Entropy Modulation for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haotian Zhao, Yuxin Zhang, Songlin Zhou, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Wenyu Zhang, Lun Tian, Tianshu Zhu, Yifeng Huang, Yucheng Zeng, Jingnan Gu, Daxiang Dong, Jianmin Wu

entry.summary: AEM introduces a supervision-free credit assignment method for multi-turn reinforcement learning of LLM agents. Adaptively modulates entropy dynamics during RL training to balance exploration-exploitation without requiring dense intermediate rewards or process reward models.

entry.title: Caracal: Causal Architecture via Spectral Mixing

author.name: Bingzheng Gan, Tianyi Zhang, Yusu Li, Jing Huang, Wei Shi, Yangkai Ding, Tao Yu

entry.summary: Caracal replaces attention with a Multi-Head Fourier module achieving O(L log L) complexity. Uses FFT for sequence mixing with frequency-domain causal masking via asymmetric padding and truncation. Hardware-agnostic and parameter-efficient.

entry.title: Social Bias in LLM-Generated Code: Benchmark and Mitigation

author.name: Fazle Rabbi, Lin Ling, Song Wang, Jinqiu Yang

entry.summary: Comprehensive study of social bias in LLM-generated code using SocialBias-Bench (343 real-world tasks, 7 demographic dimensions). Finds severe bias across all models (up to 60.58%) and that standard interventions like CoT and fairness personas amplify rather than reduce bias.

entry.title: Beyond Continuity: Simulation-free Reconstruction of Discrete Branching Dynamics from Single-cell Snapshots

author.name: Junda Ying, Yuxuan Wang, Bowen Yang, Peijie Zhou, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: Presents Unbalanced Schrödinger Bridge (USB), a simulation-free framework for learning cellular dynamics that models discrete birth-death events at single-cell resolution, going beyond continuous fluid assumptions of existing optimal transport methods.

entry.title: When RAG Chatbots Expose Their Backend: An Anonymized Case Study of Privacy and Security Risks in Patient-Facing Medical AI

author.name: Alfredo Madrid-Garc\'ia, Miguel Rujas

entry.summary: Reports a security assessment of a patient-facing medical RAG chatbot revealing privacy and security vulnerabilities, providing governance lessons for deploying generative AI in healthcare.

entry.title: StyleShield: Exposing the Fragility of AIGC Detectors through Continuous Controllable Style Transfer

author.name: Guantian Zheng

entry.summary: Presents StyleShield, a flow matching framework for conditional text style transfer that exposes the fragility of AIGC detectors by showing the statistical boundary between AI and human writing dissolves as models improve.

entry.title: LEAP: Layer-wise Exit-Aware Pretraining for Efficient Transformer Inference

author.name: Shashank Kapadia, Deep Naryan Mishra, Sujal Reddy Alugubelli, Haoan Wang, Saipraveen Vabbilisetty, Rishi Bhatia, Anupriya Sharma

entry.summary: Introduces LEAP, an auxiliary training objective that reconciles layer-aligned distillation with convergence-based early exit for efficient transformer inference, resolving their systematic incompatibility.

entry.title: Linear-Readout Floors and Threshold Recovery in Computation in Superposition

author.name: Hector Borobia, Elies Segu\'i-Mas, Guillermina Tormo-Carb\'o

entry.summary: Clarifies the apparent contradiction between two approaches to computation in superposition (O(d^{3/2}) vs near-quadratic capacity) by showing they maintain different interface invariants, and proves a Welch-type lower bound for linear readouts.

entry.title: Activation Compression in LLMs: Theoretical Analysis and Efficient Algorithm

author.name: Wen-Da Wei, Han-Bin Fang, Yang-Di Liu, Jiang-Xin Shi, James Kwok, Yu-Feng Li

entry.summary: Develops theoretical framework showing activation compression is safe for linear operators but problematic for nonlinear ones in LLM training, with convergence guarantees under L-smoothness assumptions.

entry.title: Barriers to Counterfactual Credit Attribution for Autoregressive Models

author.name: Aloni Cohen, Chenhao Zhang

entry.summary: Studies counterfactual credit attribution for autoregressive generative models, showing barriers to two natural approaches: per-token CCA doesn't compose to sequence-level CCA, and natural sequence-level CCA conflicts with RAG utility.

entry.title: AI Alignment via Incentives and Correction

author.name: Rohit Agarwal, Joshua Lin, Mark Braverman, Elad Hazan

entry.summary: Studies AI alignment through law-and-economics deterrence models, treating misalignment as strategic response to incentives and framing alignment as a fixed-point problem between solver misbehavior and auditor inspection incentives.

entry.title: Molecular Representations for Large Language Models

author.name: Nicholas T. Runcie, Fergus Imrie, Charlotte M. Deane

entry.summary: Introduces MolJSON, a novel molecular representation for LLMs, and systematically compares it with five chemical formats across GPT-5-nano/mini/5 and Claude Haiku 4.5, evaluating which representations enable reliable molecular reasoning.

entry.title: Flexi-LoRA with Input-Adaptive Ranks: Efficient Finetuning for Speech and Reasoning Tasks

author.name: Zongqian Li, Yixuan Su, Han Zhou, Zihao Fu, Nigel Collier

entry.summary: Flexi-LoRA dynamically adjusts LoRA ranks based on input complexity during both training and inference. Demonstrates that consistency between training and inference dynamics matters, especially for sequential reasoning tasks, achieving higher performance with fewer parameters.

entry.title: Bridging the Gap Between Average and Discounted TD Learning

author.name: Haoxing Tian, Zaiwei Chen, Ioannis Ch. Paschalidis, Alex Olshevsky

entry.summary: Introduces a novel algorithm for average-reward TD learning policy evaluation using two Markovian trajectories, overcoming theoretical difficulties from the non-contractive Bellman operator. Guarantees convergence without requiring direct eigenvalue estimation.

entry.title: Boundary Mass and the Soft-to-Hard Limit in Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Reza Rastegar

entry.summary: Studies the singular soft-to-hard routing limit in Mixture-of-Experts models, proving that boundary mass (probability of routing ties) is linear in slab width via coarea/tube estimates, yielding quantitative risk bounds.

entry.title: KANs need curvature: penalties for compositional smoothness

author.name: James Bagrow

entry.summary: Derives a basis-agnostic curvature penalty for Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) to prevent pathologically oscillatory activations while maintaining accuracy. Proves bounds on full model curvature relative to the penalty term.

entry.title: When Attention Collapses: Residual Evidence Modeling for Compositional Inference

author.name: Niklas Houba

entry.summary: Identifies 'slot collapse' in attention-based models under additive superposition where multiple slots converge to the same dominant component. Proposes Residual Evidence Modeling that accounts for already-explained evidence to prevent this failure mode.

entry.title: Gradient-Gated DPO: Stabilizing Preference Optimization in Language Models

author.name: Inoussa Mouiche

entry.summary: Gate-DPO introduces gradient gating to stabilize DPO training by addressing the squeezing effect where negative gradients on rejected responses cause probability collapse on high-confidence predictions.

entry.title: CLEAR: Revealing How Noise and Ambiguity Degrade Reliability in LLMs for Medicine

author.name: Kevin H. Guo, Chao Yan, Avinash Baidya, Katherine Brown, Xiang Goa, Juming Xiong, Zhijun Yin, Bradley A. Malin

entry.summary: Introduces CLEAR, a framework that assesses how decision-space presentation, ambiguity, and uncertainty affect LLM reasoning on medical benchmarks. Reveals that increasing plausible answers degrades performance and that models resist abstention, exposing limitations of exam-style evaluation.

entry.title: SplitZip: Ultra Fast Lossless KV Compression for Disaggregated LLM Serving

author.name: Yipin Guo, Siddharth Joshi

entry.summary: SplitZip proposes ultra-fast lossless KV cache compression for disaggregated LLM serving, addressing the transfer bottleneck between prefill and decode workers. Targets long-input and agentic workloads.

entry.title: Submodular Benchmark Selection

author.name: Alexander Smola

entry.summary: Formalizes LLM benchmark subset selection as submodular maximization, comparing entropy and mutual information objectives. Shows mutual information selection outperforms entropy for imputation at small subsets.

entry.title: VideoNet: A Large-Scale Dataset for Domain-Specific Action Recognition

author.name: Tanush Yadav, Mohammadreza Salehi, Jae Sung Park, Vivek Ramanujan, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Yejin Choi, Ali Farhadi, Rohun Tripathi, Ranjay Krishna

entry.summary: Introduces VideoNet, a domain-specific action recognition benchmark covering 1,000 distinct actions from 37 domains, revealing large gaps between closed and open VLMs (Gemini 3.1 Pro: 63% vs GPT-5.4: 43%).

entry.title: Component-Aware Self-Speculative Decoding in Hybrid Language Models

author.name: Hector Borobia, Elies Segu\'i-Mas, Guillermina Tormo-Carb\'o

entry.summary: Introduces the first self-speculative decoding method that exploits internal architectural heterogeneity of hybrid language models (SSM/attention), using the SSM subgraph as a zero-cost internal draft.

entry.title: Medmarks: A Comprehensive Open-Source LLM Benchmark Suite for Medical Tasks

author.name: Benjamin Warner, Ratna Sagari Grandhi, Max Kieffer, Aymane Ouraq, Saurav Panigrahi, Geetu Ambwani, Kunal Bagga, Nikhil Khandekar, Arya Hariharan, Nishant Mishra, Manish Ram, Shamus Sim Zi Yang, Ahmed Essouaied, Adepoju Jeremiah Moyondafoluwa, Robert Scholz, Bofeng Huang, Molly Beavers, Srishti Gureja, Anish Mahishi, Sameed Khan, Maxime Griot, Hunar Batra, Jean-Benoit Delbrouck, Siddhant Bharadwaj, Ronald Clark, Ashish Vashist, Anas Zafar, Leema Krishna Murali, Harsh Deshpande, Ameen Patel, William Brown, Johannes Hagemann, Connor Lane, Paul Steven Scotti, Tanishq Mathew Abraham

entry.summary: Medmarks is a fully open-source medical LLM evaluation suite with 30 benchmarks spanning diverse medical tasks, evaluating 61 models including frontier reasoning models (Gemini 3 Pro, GPT-5.1, GPT-5.2).

entry.title: Automated Interpretability and Feature Discovery in Language Models with Agents

author.name: Arnau Marin-Llobet, Javier Ferrando

entry.summary: Introduces an autonomous multi-agent framework for mechanistic interpretability that automates both explaining and discovering internal features in LLMs through iterative hypothesis testing and activation-space analysis.

entry.title: What Single-Prompt Accuracy Misses: A Multi-Variant Reliability Audit of Language Models

author.name: Ranit Karmakar, Jayita Chatterjee

entry.summary: Audits 15 open-weight language models across multiple prompt variants, revealing that single-prompt accuracy misses important reliability failures. Finds that evaluation design choices (like ECE normalization) can materially change conclusions, and that models show significant prompt-perturbation sensitivity.

entry.title: MolViBench: Evaluating LLMs on Molecular Vibe Coding

author.name: Jiatong Li, Yuxuan Ren, Weida Wang, Changmeng Zheng, Xiao-yong Wei, Qing Li, Yatao Bian

entry.summary: Introduces MolViBench, a benchmark evaluating LLMs on 'molecular vibe coding' - the paradigm where chemists interact with LLMs to generate executable programs for molecular tasks. Bridges the gap between general code generation benchmarks and chemistry-focused knowledge benchmarks.

entry.title: Chain of Evidence: Pixel-Level Visual Attribution for Iterative Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Peiyang Liu, Ziqiang Cui, Xi Wang, Di Liang, Wei Ye

entry.summary: Presents Chain of Evidence (CoE), a visual attribution framework for iterative RAG that provides pixel-level evidence localization rather than coarse text-level citations. Addresses visual semantic loss when converting rich documents to text.

entry.title: SignVerse-2M: A Two-Million-Clip Pose-Native Universe of 25+ Sign Languages

author.name: Sen Fang, Hongbin Zhong, Yanxin Zhang, Dimitris N. Metaxas

entry.summary: Presents SignVerse-2M, a two-million-clip pose-native dataset covering 25+ sign languages. Provides unified keypoint representations compatible with modern pose-driven generation frameworks, addressing limitations of RGB-based approaches.

entry.title: Adversarial Flow Matching for Imperceptible Attacks on End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Xinyu Zeng, Xiangkun He, Lei Tao, Chen Lv, Hong Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes adversarial flow matching to generate imperceptible perturbations that can manipulate end-to-end autonomous driving models (both VLA and modular architectures) by targeting shared Transformer vulnerabilities, without requiring full model access.

entry.title: Rethink MAE with Linear Time-Invariant Dynamics

author.name: Zice Wang

entry.summary: Proposes SSMProbe, using State Space Models as permutation-sensitive probes for visual representations, demonstrating that token order is a critical exploitable dimension in frozen ViT representations. Formulates token ordering as an information scheduling problem.

entry.title: Beyond Perceptual Shortcuts: Causal-Inspired Debiasing Optimization for Generalizable Video Reasoning in Lightweight MLLMs

author.name: Jingze Wu, Quan Zhang, Hongfei Suo, Zeqiang Cai, Hongbo Chen

entry.summary: Proposes VideoThinker, a causal-inspired framework that addresses 'perceptual bias' in RL-finetuned lightweight MLLMs, showing that RL drives models to use perceptual shortcuts rather than genuine reasoning. Uses two-stage debiasing.

entry.title: Act2See: Emergent Active Visual Perception for Video Reasoning

author.name: Martin Q. Ma, Yuxiao Qu, Aditya Agrawal, Willis Guo, Paul Pu Liang, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, Louis-Philippe Morency

entry.summary: Act2See enables VLMs to actively interleave video frame retrieval within chain-of-thought reasoning for video understanding, rather than relying on static initial frames. The framework is trained via SFT on reasoning traces from a frontier VLM that integrate active perception actions.

entry.title: Validation of an AI-based end-to-end model for prostate pathology using long-term archived routine samples

author.name: Xiaoyi Ji, Renata Zelic, Oskar Aspegren, Nita Mulliqi, Michelangelo Fiorentino, Francesca Giunchi, Luca Molinaro, Sol Erika Boman, Lorenzo Richiardi, Andreas Pettersson, Per Henrik Vincent, Martin Eklund, Olof Akre, Kimmo Kartasalo

entry.summary: Validates GleasonAI, an end-to-end AI model for prostate pathology grading, on 10,366 biopsy cores from 1,028 patients across 14 Swedish regions spanning 17 years. Achieves quadratic-weighted kappa of 0.86, comparable to experienced pathologists, with stable performance across time and geography.

entry.title: Linearizing Vision Transformer with Test-Time Training

author.name: Yining Li, Dongchen Han, Zeyu Liu, Hanyi Wang, Yulin Wang, Gao Huang

entry.summary: Proposes converting pretrained Vision Transformers to linear-complexity architectures using Test-Time Training (TTT) layers, leveraging structural alignment between TTT's two-layer formulation and softmax attention for direct weight inheritance.

entry.title: Sentinel-VLA: A Metacognitive VLA Model with Active Status Monitoring for Dynamic Reasoning and Error Recovery

author.name: Wenhao Li, Xiu Su, Yichao Cao, Hongyan Xu, Xiaobo Xia, Shan You, Yi Chen, Chang Xu

entry.summary: Sentinel-VLA introduces a metacognitive VLA model with active status monitoring that triggers dynamic reasoning or error recovery only when necessary, reducing computational overhead while improving robustness.

entry.title: Latent Bridge: Feature Delta Prediction for Efficient Dual-System Vision-Language-Action Model Inference

author.name: Yudong Liu, Yuan Li, Zijia Tang, Yuxi Zheng, Yueqian Lin, Qinsi Wang, Yi Li, Shuangjun Liu, Shuai Zhang, Taotao Jing, Dashan Gao, Ning Bi, Jingwei Sun, Yiran Chen, Hai Li

entry.summary: Proposes Latent Bridge, a lightweight model that predicts VLM output deltas between timesteps for efficient dual-system VLA inference. Demonstrates on GR00T-N1.6 and π0.5, reducing VLM calls while maintaining performance across four benchmarks.

entry.title: Who Decides What Is Harmful? Content Moderation Policy Through A Multi-Agent Personalised Inference Framework

author.name: Ewelina Gajewska, Michal Wawer, Katarzyna Budzynska, Jaroslaw A. Chudziak

entry.summary: Proposes an LLM-based multi-agent personalized content moderation framework that filters content based on individual user sensitivity profiles. Combines Expert Agents, a Manager Agent, and a Ghost Profile Agent simulating user perspectives.

entry.title: VLA-ATTC: Adaptive Test-Time Compute for VLA Models with Relative Action Critic Model

author.name: Wenhao Li, Xiu Su, Dan Niu, Yichao Cao, Hongyan Xu, Zhe Qu, Lei Fan, Shan You, Chang Xu

entry.summary: VLA-ATTC introduces adaptive test-time compute for VLA models with an uncertainty-based 'cognitive clutch' that transitions from reflexive execution to deliberation, using a Relative Action Critic to select optimal actions.

entry.title: Local Hessian Spectral Filtering for Robust Intrinsic Dimension Estimation

author.name: Genki Osada

entry.summary: Proposes Local Hessian Spectral Dimension (LHSD) for estimating local intrinsic dimension using diffusion models, which applies spectral filtering to the log-density Hessian to separate tangent from normal directions. Detects memorization in large-scale diffusion models.

entry.title: EditPropBench: Measuring Factual Edit Propagation in Scientific Manuscripts

author.name: Garvin Kruthof

entry.summary: Introduces EditPropBench, a benchmark measuring whether LLM editors propagate factual edits through dependent claims in scientific manuscripts. Each item contains a synthetic manuscript, a targeted edit, and a fact graph with sentence-level labels for direct targets and downstream updates.

entry.title: AgentFloor: How Far Up the tool use Ladder Can Small Open-Weight Models Go?

author.name: Ranit Karmakar, Jayita Chatterjee

entry.summary: AgentFloor is a deterministic 30-task benchmark organized as a six-tier capability ladder for evaluating open-weight models on agentic tasks. Evaluates 16 models from 0.27B to 32B alongside GPT-5, finding clear boundaries where small models suffice and where frontier intelligence is needed.

entry.title: To Call or Not to Call: A Framework to Assess and Optimize LLM Tool Calling

author.name: Qinyuan Wu, Soumi Das, Mahsa Amani, Arijit Nag, Seungeon Lee, Krishna P. Gummadi, Abhilasha Ravichander, Muhammad Bilal Zafar

entry.summary: Introduces a decision-theory-inspired framework to evaluate whether LLMs should call web search tools, assessing necessity, utility, and affordability. Combines normative analysis with empirical evaluation of when tool use helps vs. hurts.

entry.title: CRC-Screen: Certified DNA-Synthesis Hazard Screening Under Taxonomic Shift

author.name: Najmul Hasan

entry.summary: CRC-Screen addresses DNA synthesis hazard screening failures when hazardous sequences come from taxonomic families absent from reference sets. Composes k-mer similarity, LLM judge panels, and embedding centroids under Conformal Risk Control for certified screening.

entry.title: DeGenTWeb: A First Look at LLM-dominant Websites

author.name: Sichang Steven He, Calvin Ardi, Ramesh Govindan, Harsha V. Madhyastha

entry.summary: DeGenTWeb systematically identifies LLM-dominant websites on the web, adapting LLM-generated text detectors to minimize false attributions. Finds that detectors perform much worse than advertised when trying to avoid falsely flagging human content.

entry.title: Rethinking Network Topologies for Cost-Effective Mixture-of-Experts LLM Serving

author.name: Junsun Choi, Sam Son, Sunjin Choi, Hansung Kim, Yakun Sophia Shao, Scott Shenker, Sylvia Ratnasamy, Borivoje Nikolic

entry.summary: Systematic cross-layer analysis of network topologies for MoE LLM serving, comparing scale-up, scale-out, 3D torus, and 3D full-mesh. Finds lower-cost switchless topologies improve cost-effectiveness by 20.6-56.2% over expensive scale-up networks.

entry.title: Semia: Auditing Agent Skills via Constraint-Guided Representation Synthesis

author.name: Hongbo Wen, Ying Li, Hanzhi Liu, Chaofan Shou, Yanju Chen, Yuan Tian, Yu Feng

entry.summary: Semia is a static auditor for agent skills that lifts LLM-driven agent configurations into a Datalog fact base (SDL), enabling reproducible security analysis of how prose instructions interact with executable interfaces.

entry.title: Improving LLM Code Generation via Requirement-Aware Curriculum Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shouyu Yin, Zhao Tian, Junjie Chen, Shikai Guo

entry.summary: Proposes a requirement-aware curriculum reinforcement learning strategy for LLM code generation that aligns training difficulty with actual requirement complexity, addressing limitations of existing CRL approaches.

entry.title: PAMod: Modeling Cyclical Shifts via Phase-Amplitude Modulation for Non-stationary Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Yingbo Zhou, Yutong Ye, Shuhao Li, Rui Qian, Qiang Huang, Lemao Liu, Li Sun, Dejing Dou

entry.summary: Proposes PAMod for non-stationary time series forecasting that models cyclical distribution shifts via Phase-Amplitude Modulation, addressing the assumption in RevIN that historical and future distributions are identical.

entry.title: A11y-Compressor: A Framework for Enhancing the Efficiency of GUI Agent Observations through Visual Context Reconstruction and Redundancy Reduction

author.name: Michito Takeshita, Takuro Kawada, Takumi Ohashi, Shunsuke Kitada, Hitoshi Iyatomi

entry.summary: Proposes A11y-Compressor, a framework that transforms accessibility trees into compact representations for GUI agents, reducing input tokens to 22% while maintaining or improving task performance on OSWorld benchmark.

entry.title: Possibilistic Predictive Uncertainty for Deep Learning

author.name: Yao Ni, Jeremie Houssineau, Yew Soon Ong, Piotr Koniusz

entry.summary: Introduces DAPPr, a framework using possibility theory for epistemic uncertainty quantification in deep learning that bridges principled Bayesian approaches and efficient second-order predictors.

entry.title: Augmented Lagrangian Multiplier Network for State-wise Safety in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jiaming Zhang, Yujie Yang, Yao Lyu, Shengbo Eben Li, Liping Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes an augmented Lagrangian multiplier network for state-wise safety constraints in RL, addressing training oscillations caused by network generalization propagating local overshoots to adjacent states.

entry.title: Watch Your Step: Information Injection in Diffusion Models via Shadow Timestep Embedding

author.name: An Huang, Junggab Son, Zuobin Xiong

entry.summary: Introduces Shadow Timestep Embedding (STE), a mechanism for injecting information into diffusion models through the underutilized timestep embedding space, highlighting security risks and potential for provenance.

entry.title: GEODE: Angle-Adaptive OOD Detection with Universal Scorer Compatibility

author.name: Bruno Abrahao

entry.summary: Introduces GEODE for OOD detection that replicates Outlier Exposure's boundary calibration effect synthetically through angle-adaptive norm loss, with theoretical grounding in neural collapse.

entry.title: Learning to Race in Minutes: Infoprop Dyna on the Mini Wheelbot

author.name: Devdutt Subhasish, Henrik Hose, Sebastian Trimpe

entry.summary: Demonstrates that Infoprop Dyna, an uncertainty-aware MBRL framework, enables a unicycle robot to learn to race around a track within 11 minutes of real-world experience without simulation.

entry.title: Extreme Weather Bench: A framework and benchmark for evaluation of high-impact weather

author.name: Amy McGovern, Taylor Mandelbaum, Daniel Rothenberg, Nicholas Loveday, Corey Potvin, Montgomery Flora, Linus Magnusson, Eric Gilleland, John Allen

entry.summary: Introduces Extreme Weather Bench (EWB), a community-driven benchmark suite for evaluating AI and NWP models on high-impact weather forecasting, addressing the lack of standardized evaluation beyond global-scale metrics or cherry-picked case studies.

entry.title: Focus and Dilution: The Multi-stage Learning Process of Attention

author.name: Zheng-An Chen, Pengxiao Lin, Zhi-Qin John Xu, Tao Luo

entry.summary: Identifies and rigorously explains a recurrent focus-dilution cycle in attention learning dynamics for one-layer Transformers on Markovian data, decomposing the cycle into distinct stages with provable transitions.

entry.title: Breaking the Computational Barrier: Provably Efficient Actor-Critic for Low-Rank MDPs

author.name: Ruiquan Huang, Donghao Li, Yingbin Liang, Jing Yang

entry.summary: Establishes a computational hierarchy of RL oracles under low-rank MDPs, showing policy evaluation is most efficient, then proposes a novel optimistic actor-critic algorithm achieving both computational and sample efficiency.

entry.title: S^3-R1: Learning to Retrieve and Answer Step-by-Step with Synthetic Data

author.name: Harsh Goel, Akhil Udathu, Susmija Jabireddy, Pradnesh Kalkar, Atharva Parulekar

entry.summary: Introduces S³-R1, a framework combining synthetic multi-hop question generation with denser learning signals to improve RL-trained models for agentic search and question-answering, addressing limitations of sparse rewards.

entry.title: Decision-Focused Learning via Tangent-Space Projection of Prediction Error

author.name: Junhyeong Lee, Sangjin Jin, Yongjae Lee

entry.summary: Shows that regret gradients in decision-focused learning equal MSE gradients projected onto the tangent space of active constraints scaled by curvature, providing a closed-form geometric characterization without differentiating through solvers.

entry.title: Protein-Conditioned Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning for Full-Length mRNA Design

author.name: Zixi Shao, Tao Wang, Yibei Xiao, Tianyi Huang

entry.summary: Proposes ProMORNA, a multi-objective RL framework for designing full-length mRNA sequences from protein targets, using BART-style encoder-decoder with Multi-Objective Group Relative Policy Optimization to balance stability, translation efficiency, and immune safety.

entry.title: PRIME: Protein Representation via Physics-Informed Multiscale Equivariant Hierarchies

author.name: Viet Thanh Duy Nguyen, John K. Johnstone, Truong-Son Hy

entry.summary: Introduces PRIME, a protein representation framework modeling proteins as nested five-level structural graphs (surface to protein level) with physics-informed equivariant hierarchies for multi-scale learning.

entry.title: Stable GFlowNets with Probabilistic Guarantees

author.name: Zengxiang Lei, Ananth Shreekumar, Jonathan Rosenthal, Ruoyu Song, Alvaro A. Cardenas, Daniel J. Fremont, Dongyan Xu, Satish Ukkusuri, Z. Berkay Celik

entry.summary: Proposes Stable GFlowNets with theoretical analysis showing small TV distance doesn't preclude unbounded loss, derives loss-to-TV bounds, and provides a stabilization algorithm with probabilistic guarantees.

entry.title: Mitigating Multimodal LLMs Hallucinations via Relevance Propagation at Inference Time

author.name: Itai Allouche, Joseph Keshet

entry.summary: Proposes LIME, a training-free framework to mitigate multimodal LLM hallucinations by using relevance propagation to enhance the influence of perceptual inputs during inference, addressing the imbalance between text and visual modalities.

entry.title: Skipping the Zeros in Diffusion Models for Sparse Data Generation

author.name: Phil Sidney Ostheimer, Mayank Nagda, Andriy Balinskyy, Gabriel Vicente Rodrigues, Jean Radig, Carl Herrmann, Stephan Mandt, Marius Kloft, Sophie Fellenz

entry.summary: Proposes Sparsity-Exploiting Diffusion (SED) that models only non-zero values in sparse data, preserving sparsity patterns and providing computational savings while maintaining or improving generation quality across physics and biology benchmarks.

entry.title: Pandora's Regret: A Proper Scoring Rule for Evaluating Sequential Search

author.name: Gerardo A. Flores, Yash Deshpande, Jannis R. Brea, Ashia C. Wilson

entry.summary: Derives Pandora's Regret, a strictly proper scoring rule for evaluating sequential search that penalizes rank-reversing miscalibrations where distractors outrank the true class. Shows that sequential search induces pairwise structure that overcomes limitations of standard local scoring rules like log loss.

entry.title: MER-DG: Modality-Entropy Regularization for Multimodal Domain Generalization

author.name: Yavuz Yarici, Ghassan AlRegib

entry.summary: MER-DG identifies 'Fusion Overfitting' in multimodal domain generalization where encoders exploit cross-modal co-occurrences from source-specific recording conditions rather than learning domain-invariant features. Proposes modality-entropy regularization to address this.

entry.title: Bringing Order to Asynchronous SGD: Towards Optimality under Data-Dependent Delays with Momentum

author.name: Tehila Dahan, Roie Reshef, Sharon Goldstein, Kfir Y. Levy

entry.summary: Proposes a momentum-based asynchronous SGD framework that preserves information from delayed gradients rather than discarding them, addressing systematic bias from data-dependent delays. Achieves near-optimal rates in the smooth convex case.

entry.title: Weight Clipping for Robust Conformal Inference under Unbounded Covariate Shifts

author.name: James Wang, Surbhi Goel

entry.summary: Introduces clipped least-squares importance fitting (CLISF) for robust conformal prediction under unbounded covariate shifts, addressing both overfitting in density ratio estimation and high variance in threshold estimation.

entry.title: Detecting Adversarial Data via Provable Adversarial Noise Amplification

author.name: Furkan Mumcu, Yasin Yilmaz

entry.summary: Provides a formal adversarial noise amplification theorem with sufficient conditions, then proposes a training methodology with spectral loss and architectural design to enhance amplification signals for detecting adversarial inputs.

entry.title: STABLEVAL: Disagreement-Aware and Stable Evaluation of AI Systems

author.name: Akash Bonagiri, Gerard Janno Anderias, Saee Patil, Angelina Lai, Devang Borkar, Gezheng Kang, Ishant Gandhi, Setareh Rafatirad, Houman Homayoun

entry.summary: STABLEVAL introduces a disagreement-aware evaluation framework that models latent item correctness and annotator-specific confusion patterns to produce calibrated agent-level scores, addressing instability from majority vote aggregation in AI evaluation.

entry.title: Manifold-Constrained Adversarial Training for Long-Tailed Robustness via Geometric Alignment

author.name: Guanmeng Xian, Ning Yang, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: MCAT proposes manifold-constrained adversarial training for long-tailed distributions, penalizing deviations from class-conditional manifolds and using ETF-inspired regularization for balanced geometric separation. Provides theoretical links between geometric separation and robust margins.

entry.title: A Near-optimal SQ Lower Bound for Smoothed Agnostic Learning of Boolean Halfspaces

author.name: Tim Sinen

entry.summary: Proves a near-optimal statistical query lower bound for smoothed agnostic learning of Boolean halfspaces under uniform distribution, matching the upper bound achieved by L1 polynomial regression up to logarithmic factors.

entry.title: Pretraining on Sleep Data Improves non-Sleep Biosignal Tasks

author.name: William Lehn-Schi{\o}ler, Magnus Ruud Kj{\ae}r, Phillip Hempel, Magnus Guldberg Pedersen, Rahul Thapa, Bryan He, Nicolai Spicher, Andreas Brink-Kjaer, Lars Kai Hansen, Emmanuel Mignot

entry.summary: Shows that sleep foundation models pretrained with multimodal contrastive learning on polysomnography data transfer effectively to non-sleep EEG and ECG tasks, consistently improving across eight downstream tasks.

entry.title: Earth System Foundation Model (ESFM): A unified framework for heterogeneous data integration and forecasting

author.name: Firat Ozdemir, Yun Cheng, Salman Mohebi, Fanny Lehmann, Simon Adamov, Zhenyi Zhang, Leonardo Trentini, Dana Grund, Oliver Fuhrer, Torsten Hoefler, Siddhartha Mishra, Sebastian Schemm, Benedikt Soja, Mathieu Salzmann

entry.summary: Introduces ESFM, a fully open Earth System Foundation Model built on 3D Swin UNet that handles diverse datasets including satellite data with missing values and station data under one backbone. Extends encoding schemes for heterogeneous data integration in climate sciences.

entry.title: When Embedding-Based Defenses Fail: Rethinking Safety in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Lingxi Zhang, Guangtao Zheng, Hanjie Chen

entry.summary: Demonstrates that embedding-based defenses in LLM multi-agent systems fail when attackers craft messages whose embeddings lie close to benign ones. Proposes three attack strategies (Slow Drift, Benign Wrapper, Chameleon) and analyzes the theoretical failure mode.

entry.title: Segment-Aligned Policy Optimization for Multi-Modal Reasoning

author.name: Lei Gao, Zhuoming Li, Mengxi Jia, Jiakang Yuan, Hongbo Sun, Hao Sun, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: Proposes Segment-Aligned Policy Optimization (SAPO), which treats coherent reasoning steps rather than tokens or full sequences as the fundamental unit for RL policy updates in multi-modal reasoning, with segment-level value estimation and advantage computation.

entry.title: Self-Normalized Martingales and Uniform Regret Bounds for Linear Regression

author.name: Fan Chen, Jian Qian, Alexander Rakhlin, Nikita Zhivotovskiy

entry.summary: Characterizes when scale-invariant upper bounds on self-normalized martingales are possible, proving they exist only in dimension d=1 without further assumptions. Provides O(log T) bounds in d=1 and new uniform regret bounds for linear regression.

entry.title: Principles and Guidelines for Randomized Controlled Trials in AI Evaluation

author.name: Christopher Kelly, Angelica Chowdhury, Alexandra Campili, Bimpe Ayoola, Devin Barbour, Thomas Chen Dawson, Ze Shen Chin, Rokas Gipi\v{s}kis

entry.summary: Establishes a framework for standardizing AI evaluation RCTs (human uplift studies), operationalizing five principles into 33 guidelines adapted from established experimental disciplines.

entry.title: A Parameter-Free First-Order Algorithm for Non-Convex Optimization with $\tilde{\mkern1mu O}(\epsilon^{-5/3})$ Global Rate

author.name: Sichao Xiong, Sadok Jerad, Coralia Cartis

entry.summary: PF-AGD is the first parameter-free, deterministic accelerated first-order method achieving O(ε^{-5/3}log(1/ε)) oracle complexity for smooth non-convex optimization without requiring knowledge of smoothness constants.

entry.title: The Causal Description Gap: Information-Theoretic Separations Across Pearl's Hierarchy

author.name: Seyed Morteza Emadi

entry.summary: Formalizes the 'Causal Description Gap' via Kolmogorov complexity, showing that observational distributions can have constant description length while interventional answers require Θ(n²) bits, quantifying Pearl's hierarchy separation.

entry.title: A Theoretical Game of Attacks via Compositional Skills

author.name: Xinbo Wu, Huan Zhang, Abhishek Umrawal, Lav R. Varshney

entry.summary: Formalizes a game-theoretic framework between attackers and defenders for LLM adversarial prompting, characterizes equilibria, and reveals inherent attacker advantages while deriving provably optimal defense strategies.

entry.title: LLM Output Detectability and Task Performance Can be Jointly Optimized

author.name: Koshiro Saito, Ryuto Koike, Masahiro Kaneko, Naoaki Okazaki

entry.summary: PUPPET uses reinforcement learning to jointly optimize LLM watermark detectability and downstream task performance, showing these objectives can be harmonized rather than traded off.

entry.title: MultiBreak: A Scalable and Diverse Multi-turn Jailbreak Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Safety

author.name: Jialin Song, Xiaodong Liu, Weiwei Yang, Wuyang Chen, Mingqian Feng, Xuekai Zhu, Jianfeng Gao

entry.summary: MultiBreak is a large-scale multi-turn jailbreak benchmark (10,389 prompts, 2,665 intents) with an active learning pipeline for generating diverse adversarial prompts that iteratively fine-tunes a generator.

entry.title: The Reasoning Trap: An Information-Theoretic Bound on Closed-System Multi-Step LLM Reasoning

author.name: Kwan Soo Shin

entry.summary: The Reasoning Trap: shows that multi-agent debate produces diverse phrasings but not diverse perspectives, with an information-theoretic framework explaining why closed-system reasoning preserves accuracy while degrading reasoning quality.

entry.title: Do Large Language Models Plan Answer Positions? Position Bias in Multiple-Choice Question Generation

author.name: Xuemei Tang, Xufeng Duan, Zhenguang G. Cai

entry.summary: Demonstrates that LLMs exhibit systematic position biases when generating multiple-choice questions, with similar patterns within model families. Probing experiments reveal that hidden representations in question stems encode predictive signals of correct answer positions, suggesting implicit planning during generation.

entry.title: HalluScan: A Systematic Benchmark for Detecting and Mitigating Hallucinations in Instruction-Following LLMs

author.name: Ahmed Cherif

entry.summary: Presents HalluScan, a benchmark framework evaluating hallucination detection across 72 configurations spanning 6 detection methods, 4 model families, and 3 domains. Introduces HalluScore metric and Adaptive Detection Routing algorithm.

entry.title: Synthetic Users, Real Differences: an Evaluation Framework for User Simulation in Multi-Turn Conversations

author.name: Yu Lu Liu, Hyokun Yun, Tanya Roosta, Ziang Xiao

entry.summary: Proposes realsim, an evaluation framework for user simulation in multi-turn conversations that takes a distributional view comparing real vs. simulated dialogues along 8 dimensions covering communicative functions and user behavior.

entry.title: Energy-Based Constraint Networks: Learning Structural Coherence Across Modalities

author.name: Chirag Shinde

entry.summary: Introduces energy-based constraint networks that learn structural coherence from contrastive pairs. Uses frozen encoder embeddings through a state-space model with dual-head attention, achieving 93.4% accuracy on trained corruption types and 87.2% on unseen types.

entry.title: MedMosaic: A Challenging Large Scale Benchmark of Diverse Medical Audio

author.name: Harshit Rajgarhia, Shuubham Ojha, Asif Shaik, Akhil Pothanapalli, Rachuri Lokesh, Abhishek Mukherji, Prasanna Desikan

entry.summary: Presents MedMosaic, a medical audio QA dataset with 46,701 question-answer pairs spanning physiological sounds, synthetic speech artifacts, and clinical conversations of varying lengths for benchmarking audio reasoning models.

entry.title: Led to Mislead: Adversarial Content Injection for Attacks on Neural Ranking Models

author.name: Amin Bigdeli, Amir Khosrojerdi, Radin Hamidi Rad, Morteza Zihayat, Charles L. A. Clarke, Ebrahim Bagheri

entry.summary: Proposes CRAFT, a supervised framework for black-box adversarial rank attacks on neural ranking models using LLMs. Uses three stages: adversarial dataset generation via RAG, supervised fine-tuning, and preference-guided optimization.

entry.title: Fight Poison with Poison: Enhancing Robustness in Few-shot Machine-Generated Text Detection with Adversarial Training

author.name: Wenjing Duan, Qi Zhou, Yuanfan Li

entry.summary: Proposes REACT, an adversarial training framework that improves few-shot machine-generated text detection by coupling a humanization-oriented attacker with a contrastive detector. Uses RAG-guided attacks to strengthen detection robustness.

entry.title: LiteVLA-H: Dual-Rate Vision-Language-Action Inference for Onboard Aerial Guidance and Semantic Perception

author.name: Justn williams, Kishor Datta Gupta, Roy George, Mrinmoy Sarkar

entry.summary: Presents LiteVLA-H, a compact 256M-parameter vision-language-action system for drones, designed for dual-rate operation on edge hardware (Jetson AGX Orin) with fast guidance mode and slower semantic mode. Key finding: latency is dominated by multimodal pre-fill, not decoding.

entry.title: Disciplined Diffusion: Text-to-Image Diffusion Model against NSFW Generation

author.name: Chi Zhang, Changjia Zhu, Xiaowen Li, Yao Liu, Zhuo Lu

entry.summary: Proposes DDiffusion (Disciplined Diffusion), a text-to-image diffusion model that handles NSFW inputs by degrading harmful content quality rather than binary blocking, making it more robust to adversarial prompt manipulation.

entry.title: Unifying Deep Stochastic Processes for Image Enhancement

author.name: Wojciech Koz{\l}owski, Rados{\l}aw Kuczba\'nski, Kamil Adamczewski, Karol Szczypkowski, Maciej Zi\k{e}ba

entry.summary: Provides a unified theoretical perspective on stochastic image enhancement methods, showing that unconditional diffusion, Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes, and diffusion bridges all arise from a common SDE formulation.

entry.title: Video Active Perception: Effective Inference-Time Long-Form Video Understanding with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Martin Q. Ma, Willis Guo, Aditya Agrawal, Ankit Gupta, Paul Pu Liang, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, Louis-Philippe Morency

entry.summary: Video Active Perception (VAP) is a training-free method that enhances long-form video QA by treating keyframe selection as data acquisition, using a text-conditioned video generation model to represent prior world knowledge. Achieves SOTA zero-shot results on video QA benchmarks.

entry.title: TrajShield: Trajectory-Level Safety Mediation for Defending Text-to-Video Models Against Jailbreak Attacks

author.name: Quanchen Zou, Nizhang Li, Wenxin Zhang, Jiaye Lin, Yangchen Zeng, Xiangzheng Zhang, Zonghao Ying

entry.summary: TrajShield proposes trajectory-level safety mediation for text-to-video models, addressing temporally emergent risk where benign prompts lead to unsafe content through temporal extrapolation. Training-free and inference-time approach.

entry.title: Embody4D: A Generalist 4D World Model for Embodied AI

author.name: Peiyan Tu, Hanxin Zhu, Jingwen Sun, Shaojie Ren, Cong Wang, Jiayi Luo, Xiaoqian Cheng, Zhibo Chen

entry.summary: Embody4D proposes a video-to-video world model for embodied scenarios that synthesizes arbitrary novel views from monocular video, addressing data scarcity through 3D-aware compositional augmentation and maintaining spatiotemporal consistency.

entry.title: CADFS: A Big CAD Program Dataset and Framework for Computer-Aided Design with Large Language Models

author.name: Vladislav Pyatov, Gleb Bobrovskikh, Saveliy Galochkin, Nikita Boldyrev, Oleg Voynov, Alexander Filippov, Gonzalo Ferrer, Peter Wonka, Evgeny Burnaev

entry.summary: CADFS introduces a FeatureScript-based representation and 450k CAD model dataset spanning 15 operations for training VLMs to generate complex CAD design histories, going beyond simple sketch-extrude operations.

entry.title: Seeing Realism from Simulation: Efficient Video Transfer for Vision-Language-Action Data Augmentation

author.name: Chenyu Hui, Xiaodi Huang, Siyu Xu, Yunke Wang, Shan You, Fei Wang, Tao Huang, Chang Xu

entry.summary: Presents a framework that converts simulated VLA videos into realistic training videos while preserving task semantics and action trajectories, using video segmentation, captioning, and conditional video transfer to bridge the sim-to-real gap.

entry.title: BRITE: A Benchmark for Reliable and Interpretable T2V Evaluation on Implausible Scenarios

author.name: Advait Tilak, Jiwon Choi, Nazifa Mouli, Wei Le

entry.summary: BRITE introduces the first text-to-video evaluation benchmark that unifies implausible prompting, audio-visual consistency assessment, and QA-based interpretable evaluation, testing models including Sora 2, Veo 3.1, and Runway Gen4.5.

entry.title: Hydra-DP3: Frequency-Aware Right-Sizing of 3D Diffusion Policies for Visuomotor Control

author.name: Jinhao Zhang, Zhexuan Zhou, Huizhe Li, Yichen Lai, Wenlong Xia, Haoming Song, Youmin Gong, Jie Mei

entry.summary: Proposes Hydra-DP3, a compact diffusion policy for robot manipulation based on the insight that robot action trajectories are smooth with energy concentrated in low-frequency DCT modes. Shows that action denoising requires far fewer reverse steps and simpler models than image generation.

entry.title: AI Industrial Takeoff — Part 1: Maximum growth rates with current technology

author.name: djbinder

entry.summary: Quantitative analysis of maximum AI-driven economic growth rates using US input-output data. Finds a fully automated AI economy could double in about a year, driven by the speed of physical capital self-reproduction.

entry.title: CombinationTS: A Modular Framework for Understanding Time-Series Forecasting Models

author.name: Xiaorui Wang, Fanda Fan, Chenxi Wang, Yuxuan Yang, Rui Tang, Kuoyu Gao, Simiao Pang, Yuanfeng Shang, Zhipeng Liu, Wanling Gao, Lei Wang, Jianfeng Zhan

entry.summary: Proposes CombinationTS, a modular framework that decomposes time-series forecasting models into orthogonal components and evaluates each via marginalized performance and stability, enabling attribution of performance gains to specific modules rather than whole architectures.

entry.title: Divide and Conquer: Decoupled Representation Alignment for Multimodal World Models

author.name: Junyuan Xiao, Dingkang Liang, Xin Zhou, Yixuan Ye, Tongtong Su, Guangmo Yi, Bin Xia, Qiang Lyu, Shurui Shi, Jun Huang, Jianlou Si, Wenming Yang

entry.summary: M²-REPA proposes the first representation alignment method for multi-modal video generation, decoupling modality-specific features and aligning each with corresponding expert foundation models to leverage their domain-specific priors.

entry.title: Online Safety Filter for Deformable Object Manipulation with Horizon Agnostic Neural Operators

author.name: Jiaxing Li, Hanjiang Hu, Zhuoyuan Wang, Yorie Nakahira, Changliu Liu

entry.summary: Presents a horizon-agnostic neural operator as an online safety filter for deformable object manipulation that enforces explicit task-level safety constraints in real time by minimally modifying any nominal control policy.

entry.title: ARMOR 2025: A Military-Aligned Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Model Safety Beyond Civilian Contexts

author.name: Sydney Johns, Heng Jin, Chaoyu Zhang, Y. Thomas Hou, Wenjing Lou

entry.summary: Introduces ARMOR 2025, a benchmark for evaluating LLM safety in military contexts, grounded in Law of War, Rules of Engagement, and Joint Ethics Regulation. Addresses a gap where existing safety benchmarks focus on civilian risks but don't test military doctrinal compliance.

entry.title: Exploring LLM biases to manipulate AI search overview

author.name: Roman Smirnov

entry.summary: Investigates biases in LLM-based search overview systems and trains a small model to exploit these biases to manipulate search results. Demonstrates that both source selection and answer generation stages are affected by LLM biases.

entry.title: When Do Diffusion Models learn to Generate Multiple Objects?

author.name: Yujin Jeong, Arnas Uselis, Iro Laina, Seong Joon Oh, Anna Rohrbach

entry.summary: Studies when diffusion models learn to generate multiple objects, separating data effects through concept generalization (imbalanced distributions) and compositional generalization (held-out combinations). Introduces mosaic framework for controlled study.

entry.title: RadLite: Multi-Task LoRA Fine-Tuning of Small Language Models for CPU-Deployable Radiology AI

author.name: Pankaj Gupta, Kartik Bose

entry.summary: Demonstrates that small language models (3-4B parameters) can achieve strong multi-task radiology performance through LoRA fine-tuning, enabling CPU deployment. Trains on 162K samples spanning 9 radiology tasks across 12 public datasets.

entry.title: Empowering Heterogeneous Graph Foundation Models via Decoupled Relation Alignment

author.name: Ziyu Zheng, Yaming Yang, Zhe Wang, Ziyu Guan, Wei Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes DRSA, a plug-and-play relation-driven alignment framework for heterogeneous graph foundation models that decouples feature semantics from relation structures to avoid type collapse and relation confusion.

entry.title: EASE: Federated Multimodal Unlearning via Entanglement-Aware Anchor Closure

author.name: Zihao Ding, Beining Wu, Jun Huang

entry.summary: Proposes EASE for federated multimodal unlearning, identifying that cross-modal entanglement in joint embeddings creates residual anchors that prevent effective unlearning, and addressing this through anchor closure.

entry.title: CGM-JEPA: Learning Consistent Continuous Glucose Monitor Representations via Predictive Self-Supervised Pretraining
